An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of 57 pb of data from the LHCb experiment, which was collected at a 7 TeTe proton proton collision energy. A timeframe between 1.44 ns and 1.49 ns has been established at a 0.12 ns confidence level, based on 1.36 x 10^6 $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decays identified through a phase space model fit to their vertex displacement.

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth analysis of extremely high-energy cosmic-ray data from the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals a significant pattern of directional variation for energies exceeding 4 EeV. As the energy level increases, so does the measured distortion in the distribution of arrival directions. By employing a method known as spherical harmonics, we determined a 2D map of 8-sigma significance that reflects this energy-dependent anisotropy. A specific multipole axis in this map seems to correspond with the plane formed by our Milky Way and our neighboring galaxy, the Andromeda. We also compared our findings to those from the TA-Fluorescence Array, discovering a compatible pattern of anisotropy with a shared significant multipole axis. This particular axis may be related to a previously identified preferred axis of mid-energy cosmic rays.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with a centre of mass energy of 5.02 TeV and 25 nanobarns of integrated luminosity, enabling a comparison with interpolated pp measurements at 2.76 and 7 TeV. Owing to its sophisticated design and reliability, the ATLAS detector successfully collected a comprehensive dataset during heavy ion and proton-proton runs. As a result, it facilitated precise measurements of the nuclear modification factor, obtained by dividing charged particle yields in hadron-hadron collisions by those in proton-proton collisions, across a wide spectrum of transverse momenta and rapidities.

Quantum mechanics can be explored on noncommutative spaces, characterized by specific commutation relations that define the structure constants of a Lie algebra. By transforming the coordinates into linear differential operators in a commuting space, we can transform an noncommutative system into an equivalent commuting one. These equivalent operators satisfy similar commutation relations to their noncommutative counterparts, and are related through a Fourier-type transformation. This allows us to recover the noncommutative wave functions from their commuting equivalents. Such a mapping is also applicable to the harmonic oscillator's q-deformed versions, with different values of q representing varying degrees of noncommutativity.

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digitized tissue samples, specifically in a classification application involving the detection of tumor cells within whole-slide images. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse dataset of cancer images from various sources, we compared the results of training models using both a federated approach and a centralized approach. Our findings indicate that federated learning can produce models with similar accuracy to those trained with centralized data, while avoiding the need to share sensitive patient data.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 110 Gbit/s using the Duobinary equalization technique over a South China Sea submarine fiber link.  Unfortunately, Rayleigh scattering from splices causes a type of optical noise known as burst errors that equalizers struggle to manage effectively. To address this issue, a pre-Duobinary equalizer structure, featuring a decision feedback equalizer with opposite coefficients, was designed and analyzed both theoretically and experimentally. This modified equalizer significantly reduces the impact of burst errors by up to fourfold when combined with the traditional Duobinary equalizer, making it a promising technique for future high-speed optical communication systems.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) have gained significant popularity in the field of Time Series Forecasting (TSF). TCNs leverage a technique called dilation that allows them to process a vast amount of historical data within a short TCN depth. While effective, this technique results in inflated model parameters that hinder the accuracy and efficiency of TCNs. As a consequence, there's a need to refine TCN architecture by eliminating redundant layers and units, which can be challenging due to the disruption of continuity that dilation causes. To address this issue, we introduce a technique called Pruning In Time (PIT), which identifies and removes units with a wide range of connectivity in the temporal dimension, ensuring a more balanced level of connectivity that enhances the interpretability of the pit-optimized TCNs. To further facilitate the PIT optimization, we also develop a novel loss function that guides the removal of units with an unbalanced range of connectivity. The PIT technique is also supported by a corresponding searching operator, which enables the PIT-optimized TCNs to maintain or even enhance their performance. Through comprehensive experiments, the PIT technique demonstrates its superiority over state-of-the-art (SOTA) architecture optimization methods, resulting in significant improvements in model parameter reduction and computational efficiency, while maintaining competitive accuracy across various TSF benchmarks.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study presents initial findings on the fluctuations of flow angle and magnitude v_n, which are extracted from two-particle correlations in Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC with an energy of 5.02 TeV. The data, analyzed by ALICE, reveal the magnitude and angular fluctuations for multiple orders of v_n (3 to 8) across different collision centrality levels. Specifically, first moments show a pattern where higher v_n fluctuations correspond to higher v_n magnitudes, whereas a reverse trend is observed for v_n angle fluctuations. Notably, the data indicate a stronger dependence between v_n magnitude fluctuations and centrality for even n values (e.g., v_4, v_6, v_8) in comparison to odd n values (e.g., v_3, v_5).

The unified correspondence theory leverages the algebraic and order theoretic underpinnings of Sahlqvist correspondence to offer versatile tools for correspondence and canonicity across diverse semantic frameworks and signatures. These tools, specifically tailored to logics whose semantics rely on normal lattice expansions (DLEs), enable computation of first-order correspondents for inductive formulas using the algorithm ALBA. Conversely, our proposed method effectively employs ALBA's rules and algebraic language to reverse its computations in the DLE setting, thereby allowing the derivation of an inductive formula from its first-order correspondent.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, our work aims to explain tables that have minor inconsistencies. We specifically examine a common type of dependency known as left-linear dependencies and develop a method to identify all data patterns that would satisfy a given table, despite having some missing values. Our algorithm is efficient, running in O(n^2) time, and we also discuss its application to scenarios where the underlying data should be unique.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach can effectively capture the complex dynamics often present in count time series, enabling more accurate one-step-ahead predictions and a smoother interpretation of model parameters. Furthermore, the TV-MCAR model is shown to be mathematically equivalent to a BetaBinomial BetaNegativeBinomial dynamic model, and we have found that it addresses the limitation of lacking second-moment specification found in many other score-driven models. To evaluate the model's performance, we conducted comprehensive forecasting assessments using both simulated data and real-world economic and epidemiological time series.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
with the aim of repeating tasks on new object instances from the same category
with only a single demonstration. Achieving this goal requires the object
controller to NDFs regulate self-motion (rotation and translation) based on its
current position and orientation. To achieve this, we establish a optimization
framework where the NDFs are trained to predict rotation and translation relative
trajectories, leveraging the consistency of descriptors and poses through a
loss function. In experiments, our NDF-based object controller successfully
repeats tasks on various cups, demonstrating the capability of NDFs to capture
global properties and facilitating efficient and accurate manipulation.

The SiD Detector is one of the two validated detector designs for the future ILC, specifically tailored to meet the experimental requirements for the experiment. To better prepare for this potential facility, the SiD Collaboration has been conducting updates and R&D throughout the construction of the SiRMD at the SiD Test Facility, in order to develop key components of the detector. Given the enhanced knowledge and materials knowledge gained, the collaboration has revised the SiD Detector Concept taking into account the enhanced knowledge and materials knowledge, with the goal of reaching even better performance targets. These revisions have also led to a update on the SiD Detector baseline with the construction of the SiRMD at the SiD Test Facility.

We present the first detailed examination of the globular cluster Tz2, utilizing data from the Cluster APOgee Survey. Through high-resolution spectra obtained from APOgee and NASA's Keck/HIRES, we analyzed 33 stars around the cluster. Our study reveals that the stars in Tz2 share the same spatial location, movement patterns, chemical composition, and age. These characteristics align with those of a red giant cluster member population aged approximately 9.3 billion years old. Furthermore, the stars in Tz2 exhibit a metallicity of -0.54 and an alpha/iron ratio of +0.15, comparable to other giant clusters within the Milky Way's inner galaxy. Based on its physical properties, Tz2 is classified as a dispersed globular cluster. If Tz2 were to be considered an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, its alpha/iron ratio would be an outlier among its kind. Additionally, our study provides insights into the formation of giant clusters within the bulge region of the galaxy.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, representing an impressive compilation of research and offering a diverse range of opportunities for statistical exploration in the field of theorem proving. Despite the numerous contributions made so far, the ever-expanding nature of the archive still poses certain challenges: locating specific content has become increasingly difficult, making it essential to prioritize reuse and clarity of comprehension. This thesis proposal outlines my research objectives, which focus on these concerns, as well as initial findings, which reveal that the Isabelle Archive exhibits characteristics typical of scale-free networks, as evidenced by the distribution of node in-degrees in its dependency graph.

Using the standard Gibbs framework, we investigate the Yang-Lee singularity in classic O(N) universality classes in dimensions three or higher, by examining the zero-th magnetization moment as a function of the magnetic field. By numerically estimating the zeroth moment for various values of N and by analyzing the corresponding singular behavior, our results indicate the singularity is located at -1 for classics O(N) universality classes. Furthermore, our findings provide the first positive numerical evidence for the Yang-Lee edge singularity for the classic O(N) series in dimensions three or higher.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the optimization issues encountered in sparse signal processing. Additionally, our inequality and its derivative can be utilized to answer a question posed by Bhattarai, Doevereere, and Mondelli at the IEEE Information Theory Workshop in 2021.

Modern metasurfaces, at the intersection of advanced technology and science,  
constitute an intricate field, involving electromagnetic systems characterized by  
thin, intricate, and nonintuitive geometries.  Recent breakthroughs in  
computational design, fueled by significant advancements in hardware, software,  
and algorithms, now make it possible to analyze these complex metasurfaces  
comprehendably. This paper provides a general overview of current methods for  
computational design, with an emphasis on their underlying algorithms and  
typical implementation procedures using widely used simulation tools for  
electromagnetic analysis. By doing so, it aims to give researchers in other  
fields a clearer understanding of this dynamic and evolving area.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth vector fields with a full set of nearby first integrals, especially those at nondegenerate singular points. This theoretical validation relies heavily on key concepts, including the formal orbital linearization theorem for formally integrable vector fields, the application of the blowing-up technique, and the application of the Sternberg-Chen theorem regarding formally equivalent smooth hyperbolic vector fields.

This report outlines a deep learning approach known as the Electron Correlation
Potential Neural Network (eCPNN), which can learn simplified potential functions
that accurately capture the intricate instantaneous relationships among electrons
within complex atomic systems. Trained in an unsupervised manner with constrained
data derived from Full Configuration Interaction one-electron density functions, the
eCPNN model effectively predicts total atomic energies with remarkable precision.

We have serendipitously discovered a massive arc-like structure, which we call the Giant Arc, home to over 20 distant galaxies dating back 2.5 to 3 billion years. Nestled in the southern constellation of Scorpius, this formation spans nearly 2 billion light-years across the sky. The Giant Arc exhibits remarkable similarities to the famous Great Wall, yet it predates it by a significant margin. Using data from the SDSS and Goodson catalogs, the galaxies within the Giant Arc were identified, and its existence has been verified through cosmological simulations using the HOSMICS project. Interestingly, the distinctive morphology of the Giant Arc has also been replicated in these simulations, designating it as a genuine cosmic feature.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated, it can still provide valuable value. In the past decade, techniques based on this method have been used to achieve remarkable results. For example, in the past couple of years, based on photometric data from the APOD system, researchers were able to validate the measurements made by the APOD system and the APOD system was able to value the aerosol measurements made by the APOD system. In addition, using the photometric data from the APOD system, scientists were able to detect the seismic activity on the APOD system. While using the photometric data from the APOD system to detect the APOD system may seem like a small step, it can still provide valuable value. In order to overcome the limitations of the current methods, the APOD system needs to be validated and calibrated with the help of the photometric data from the APOD system. Recently, estimating a 6-Degree of Freedom (6DoF) object pose from a single image has gained significant interest due to its potential to unlock higher-level interpretations, such as inferring the distance and orientation of the object in the scene. Traditional methods for pose estimation can be broadly divided into two main categories: those relying on predefined 3D shape models and those utilizing shape-free approaches. Shape model-based pose estimators work by matching 2D images to their corresponding 3D model points, while shape-free methods utilize projection grouping (PG) to estimate pose. However, PG alone often falls short of accurate pose estimation. This research presents an innovative two-stage pipeline for pose estimation that integrates PG with object-image matching using deep learning techniques. In the first stage, we employ PG to create dense image projections, and in the second stage, utilize a deep learning network to learn the correspondence between 3D shapes and 2D images based on the generated data. To our knowledge, this is the first study to leverage PG data in pose estimation training. Experimental evidence demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming both PG-only and pre-shape model-based pose estimation methods on real-world data.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion in their application across multiple disciplines, due to their ability to model and track discontinuities within materials and fluids. Although various bond-based and general peridynamic models have been developed, there is currently confusion regarding their classification and comparison. This research aims to address this gap by providing a comprehensive overview of the benefits and drawbacks of peridynamic models in the context of fluid-dynamics, focusing on key aspects such as the degrees of freedom, constitutive laws, and conservation principles. The analysis will delve into specific examples from recent studies to highlight the distinctions between different models and identify areas for future research.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed, positive definite inverse matrix from a
given dataset, where the matrix can be constrained by pre-defined edges and
node-specific parameters. This technique is especially useful in applications
involving complex relationships between variables, such as electroencephalography
and genomics. Due to the absence of a closed-form solution, iterative methods
are used to arrive at a solution, and the development of efficient start-point
methods is a critical area of research. The GGLasso package provides functions
for solving the Graphical Lasso problem and exploring the graph-theoretical
underpinnings of the algorithm, enabling users to establish a head-to-tail
comparison of various graph-based start-point methods for the Algorithm of Majorization-Minimization.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations are influenced by the integration scheme's choice in how accurately they re-create the statistical behavior of the actual solution. This accurate reproduction is particularly important for large-scale simulations used in statistical mechanics and thermodynamics. This study evaluates the performance of various integration schemes under difficult conditions, such as those found in the SAMSON molecular dynamics configuration sampling method, which employs stochastic dynamics to explore the configuration space of multiple molecules simultaneously. By comparing the results, we find that implicit methods provide more efficient and accurate sampling, while among the explicit methods tested, the modified Euler method yields the best outcomes. These findings may have implications for the effectiveness ofSMC-based sampling methods in evaluating integrals through statistical mechanics.

Numerical relativity simulations allow us to study how binary black hole mergers interact with their surroundings. However, these simulations are computationally expensive, especially when involving large populations because they require high-resolution data. Consequently, compact object mergers can be represented statistically using simplified "bubble" models that describe the behavior of wave dark matter. This approach, despite being an approximation, can still provide valuable information about the environment's effect on the merger product. Building on previous work, this research develops the "burst" model, which adds the characteristic short-duration high-frequency gravitational wave signal to the original "bubble" model. This model was used in simulations of binary black hole mergers in a dark matter environment, where the specifications of the simulation were described and the results, including the characteristics of the gravitational wave signal, were analyzed using the burst-dark matter bubble model. This allows the simulation to be run at a significantly reduced computational cost, while retaining key information about the environment's effect on the merger product.

We tackle the persistent issue of exponential stability for a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped graph with three equal branches. The outer points where these branches meet are fixed while rotating. The inner point is capable of moving in two ways, with rotational movement influenced by both elasticity and friction. A detailed analysis in a Hilbert space reveals how the spectrum's asymptotic distribution and structure evolve. It demonstrates that specific eigenvector characteristics form a complete and orthonormal basis. Consequently, we derive the exponential stability of the associated semigroup directly. Notably, we show that slow-decaying eigenvectors fail to generate the entire state space. Therefore, the stabilizing friction coefficient must meet a minimum threshold to achieve the desired stability. This result has direct implications for the stability of similar elastic structures.

Researchers utilized acoustic lenses to enhance large-area photoacoustic tomography (PAT) systems by allowing detection of wide-frequency ultrasound signals generated when the subject is exposed to pulsed X-rays. However, existing lens materials, such as PTFE, suffered from poor transmission of high-energy photons, which severely limited the amount of diagnostic information that could be obtained. A novel material, PFA, was identified and characterized to see if it could serve as an effective alternative to PTFE. Experimental results showed minimal loss of diagnostic information as it passed through a 3-mm thick PFA lens, supplemented by computer simulations and a practical test demonstrating the suitability of the new material for PAT applications.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images using a learning-based approach tailored to handle these images directly, with an innovative new component that simultaneously demosaicks and deblurs them in an interpretable way. To train this model, we utilize real-world camera data transformed into synthetic raw images through a carefully designed mock camera system. Furthermore, we introduce a unique demosaicking kernel that accounts for actual camera motion, which benefits not only our proposed single-stage model but also traditional two-stage methods. Our results show our approach outperforms current state-of-the-art solutions on real camera data for the levels of motion blur and sensor noise we tested.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships. This framework is comprised of the 'cdt' package, which executes a comprehensive causal discovery process to identify the causal interactions and the causal network structure among the variables, drawing from established methodologies including those from 'Bnlearn' and 'Pcalg', in addition to pairwise algorithms like ANM. The framework is available on GitHub under the terms of the permissive MIT License.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinctive "splash dome" formation. Empirical rules describing when the splash dome closes and the point at which seal breakdown occurs have been developed, showing alignment with theoretical predictions made by Bond and my own research. A key finding within the seal breakdown duration is the discovery of a time that matches the natural oscillation period of a liquid drop, further supported by related theories made by other researchers.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover the range of universal symmetries potentially present and then investigated why they are avoided. Generalized $\theta$-terms arise in these theories, but due to their nontrivial transformation under the duality group, they can break any universal $U(1)$ symmetry.

Cloud operators frequently incorporate security hardware into their offerings to safeguard sensitive data stored on servers. However, this adds considerable overhead to data processing, prompting some researchers to explore the possibility of reducing security hardware requirements while still effectively preventing unauthorized access. Their approach involved eliminating security hardware expenses by allowing regular, unmonitored use of physically-isolated hardware, provided no sensitive data is shared with untrusted users. We present an innovative solution that makes such regular use feasible and practical through a type of hardware monitoring known as trust management. We developed an optimal hardware design that minimizes monitoring costs, proved the management's feasibility using theoretical concepts, and demonstrated its efficiency with real-world simulations. Our findings suggest that such hardware could be up to four times more cost-effective than security processors commonly used, like Intel TDX.

We investigated the challenges of robust reinforcement learning in scenarios where the reward signal is compromised by an unknown entity, even when the corruption is not deliberately malicious but rather highly significant in magnitude. We established a key limitation showing that, in the setting of Kalman control under substantial noise corruption, no robust policy can achieve a level of performance better than exponentially poor. Nevertheless, we developed a robust alternative control procedure capable of meeting the theoretical limit. Interestingly, this procedure is equivalent to applying standard, non-robust learning algorithms to altered, transformed versions of observations and rewards.

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, with the exception being Mott insulators. Further investigation using non-interacting models exposes the influential role of spin-entropic effects in cubanite, which counterbalance the tendency for electrons to occupy specific molecular orbitals.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as multi-phonon physics, is driving research into its applications in quantum acoustics. Quantum acoustics uses the quantized sound waves to control and interact with single particles, and although initial experiments showed giant Rabi oscillations between a quantum dot and a phonon, the process required an external magnetic field. These requirements hindered the creation of reliable quantum acoustics based technologies. The present study, however, shows giant Rabi oscillations between a dark exciton in a quantum dot and a longitudinal acoustic phonon without a magnetic field. The study further identifies the phonon frequency that causes the maximum oscillations and demonstrates their magnitude to be at least that of bright exciton-photon interactions. With this research, a new and robust foundation is established for developing quantum acoustics technologies, and sets the stage for exploring the development of dark exciton-phonon-based technologies.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone lattice with two types of glide symmetries in perpendicular directions using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model. This model contains horizontal and vertical hopping terms that influence different momentum regions. By adjusting the relative strengths of these hopping terms, we can achieve linear dispersion along high-symmetry paths and create two distinct Dirac cones within the same Brillouin zone under a specific ratio. A unitary transformation enables us to map this two-component lattice to a larger single-component lattice that also exhibits Dirac dispersions. These findings provide a basis for studying topological properties and exotic phenomena in this 2D lattice structure.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with detecting these states, as they vary depending on the catalytic device used. Notably, our analysis reveals that states produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers exhibit the same characteristics when analyzing the distribution of photons. We thoroughly investigate the unique quantum properties of SPCCSs, including sub-Poissonian photon statistics, reduced uncertainty, and (Squeezing) CSs, finding that they display these features with greater clarity than states similar to SPCCSs. Additionally, we determine the negative binomial and Geometric distributions that can be obtained by adjusting the input coherent state's amplitude. These distributions become indistinguishable from those of the SPCCSs under specific conditions. Notably, our states always demonstrate CS for all states with a negative binomial distribution. We also confirm that SPCCSs always possess sub-Poissonian statistics and always exhibit both sub-Poissonian and CS properties for states with amplitude $|\alpha|=1$. In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds with a vast number of atoms.

This paper presents a unified approach to solving time-varying optimization problems by directly translating system dynamics into a format suitable for computational processing. We explain how direct transcription methods work, providing a clear understanding of their application in ventilation system optimization, specifically in managing COVID-19 patients. We also outline an efficient strategy for ventilator allocation that considers the balance between effective treatment and resource management.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from medical images is a significant challenge in medical imaging due to issues with image quality and variations. Accurate segmentation of these tumors is crucial for effective treatment planning and monitoring of patient health. To achieve this, researchers analyze medical images and develop strategies to detect and segment tumors. One approach involves using manually drawn contours for precise segmentation, although this can be time-consuming and costly. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel deep learning architecture called EDAUnet, trained on CT images to efficiently identify and segment tumors in the esophagus. Experimental results demonstrate the model's performance, achieving an average Dice Similarity Coefficient of 0.713, surface distance of 3.421 mm, and Hausdorff distance of 12.51 mm.

The ongoing development of oil and gas reserves demands accurate well logging interpretation and guidance. Bayesian statistics offers a robust means of estimating unknown parameters from well log data, providing distributional outputs that reflect parameter uncertainty. By combining well log data and expert knowledge, we can create probabilistic representations of rock properties, which facilitate the quantification of uncertainty. This study presents an ensemble-based approach for well log interpretation and geosteering that accounts for uncertainty. It extends traditional deterministic methods by incorporating well log errors, downhole measurement uncertainties, and data-based error distributions. A novel ensemble-based inversion method generates multiple realizations of formation properties, reflecting uncertainty in a computationally efficient manner. These properties are used to predict well log responses and assess risks associated with downhole decisions. The proposed ensemble-based framework is applied to a real-world geosteering case, where it balances the need to stay on track with the need to maximize reservoir contact, ultimately yielding a risk-adjusted well path.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique for identifying text segments representing real-world objects or events. The complexity of NER increases with its application to other NLP tasks due to annotation errors and assumptions of non-overlapping annotation tags. The assumption is invalid for certain extraction tasks requiring identification of text segments with a specific structure, e.g., project information including nested elements like start and end times. Current extraction models struggle with such hierarchical structures, and existing NER approaches fail to capture such complex relationships. In this paper, we view nested NER as a task parsing text with a specific hierarchical structure, and propose a new model called CurrentTree that uses a tree-structured annotation tag system and a bottom-up tree parsing network to derive the final structure. Our experiments on two datasets show that our proposed model outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

We extend the use of tropical methods to counting in arithmetic settings for plane quartics, enabling a deeper understanding of the relationship between projections of integral and rational bitangents. This reveals their asymptotic equivalence and clarifies the connection between signed real bitangents and rate-limiting arithmetic bitangents. Furthermore, we provide a new tropical formula for calculating signed real bitangents, show that previous integral and rational formulas are related through appropriate extensions, and establish the universality of the tropical bitangent polynomial.

Research into the location detection of mobile nodes within wireless sensor networks is currently ongoing. We develop and test an innovative RSSI-based location finding method suitable for 802.15.4 (ZigBee) networks. To counteract the negative effects of interference from 802.11 (WiFi) signals, we design a novel approach. Our location finding method utilizes short packets transmitted at 2.45 GHz, which are less susceptible to interference than the narrower frequency band. We validate our method through comprehensive simulations and real-world tests, which show it to be highly precise, yielding an average error of under 10 cm.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, challenges, and trends in code-switching datasets spanning various domains and a wide array of language pairs. Notably, we highlight the intricacies of analyzing code-switching datasets from a sociolinguistic perspective. From this viewpoint, we contend that future work should give greater attention to understanding and documenting the contexts in which code-switching occurs. From an NLP standpoint, we suggest that current models struggle to accurately process code-switched text due to the need to tackle issues of low-resource and many-to-many mapping languages. Notably, we find that pre-trained neural machine translation models fail to effectively address code-switching without explicit fine-tuning. Furthermore, existing NLP datasets are limited in scope and lack diversity across multiple domains. As a result, we believe that creating comprehensive, multi-domain code-switched text corpora is essential for enabling robust and contextually aware NLP models.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds hold significant interest due to their optical properties used in mirror applications and their electrical insulation capabilities utilized in integrated circuits. Despite extensive research, the crystal lattice parameters of the complex and highly symmetric Ta$_2$O$_5$ remain controversial and unclear. This study aims to resolve this ambiguity by exploring a previously unexamined Ta$_2$O$_5$ symmetry using first-principles simulations and statistical sampling techniques, yielding the optimized crystal lattice parameters of 8.046 \AA, 4.296 \AA, and 3.512 \AA, in close agreement with experimental lattice parameter measurements found in the literature.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to factors such as information plausibility and user personality traits. A third crucial element, however, was identified: the "Big Geographic Sort" (BGS). This phenomenon describes the reluctance of individuals to engage with news originating from distant locations, a well-documented bias in both current society and historical periods. Utilizing Reddit discussion data from the r/factcheck and r/conspiracy subreddits between 2015 and 2019, combined with U.S. census information, our research found that local origin news significantly enhances its spread, corroborating prior findings while offering novel uses for the BGS concept in misinformation research. Additionally, the study found that the BGS effect varies by region and is diminishing over time in certain areas. These observations suggest that geographic context is a critical factor in online misinformation dissemination patterns and may be partially attributed to pre-existing conspiracy beliefs.

The advent of instant messaging, video conferencing, and mobile technology has accelerated the spread of misinformation, which poses significant risks to societal stability and national security. Despite these dangers, existing research on misinformation still lacks effectiveness due to limited ability to accurately detect and prevent its propagation. This paper aims to introduce a novel approach to detecting the spread of misinformation by analyzing patterns of word usage and propagation. Our method leverages linguistic features and dynamic information diffusion models to create a comprehensive framework for identifying suspicious events. We tested this framework on a large-scale dataset and found that it successfully detects the propagation of misinformation with high precision. Our results show that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques, offering a more efficient solution to the problem of misinformation. This research provides a potential pathway to addressing the widespread issue of misinformation by demonstrating the efficacy of our proposed detection model.

Humans employ spoken language to teach other people various skills. A study was undertaken with two objectives: first, to assess the utility of using spoken language to teach robots basic tasks involving handling objects, and second, to analyze any consistent verbal cues that human instructors commonly provide. For the study, a simple instructing system was set up where a human instructor demonstrated handling tasks to a robot receiving and learning commands via recorded speech. The results indicated that while no consistent verbal cues were commonly used, human instructors' speech generally included clear, step-by-step directions that facilitated object identification, manipulation, and purpose ID for the robot. For object ID and purpose ID, a manually created vocabulary was used, but for other features, the raw speech of the human instructors was directly applied.

Building on previous work, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees of any degree, based on a pre-specified sequence of numbers representing possible node connections. Our method allows for the generation of binary, n-ary trees, or those with various connection patterns. We demonstrate that this algorithm is both accurate and efficient, running in O(n) time with 'n' representing the number of desired nodes. Additionally, we explore potential applications of the algorithm, illustrating its use in deriving formulas by utilizing the underlying proof of correctness.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly challenging to define, especially when considering conformal symmetry. By leveraging the connection between operator product expansions and state evolution, we've established that conformal symmetry imposes specific constraints on the Fubini-Study complexity. These constraints allow us to determine the rate at which complexity grows over time for certain types of states. Notably, the universal CSW formula emerges as a direct consequence of conformal symmetry, with the initial complexity growth rate being determined by the Bekenstein bound using the perturbing operator's norm.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved significant adoption, the reliability of these systems remains untested due to the lack of comprehensive testing frameworks, particularly for conversational agents. To fill this gap, we have developed ANATCC, a robust automated testing framework that ensures the reliability of Conversational Agents through boundary value analysis, thorough input validation, and effective error handling. Furthermore, ANATCC serves as a foundation for future research aimed at enhancing the quality of Conversational Agents.

Using a sophisticated statistical method, the effective influence of a hypothetical Planet X on the currently tracked movement of the known planets is assessed. 
Based on the most precise measurements available, even a massive Planet X, with a size comparable to Neptune, positioned very close to the Sun, with a semi-major axis of 5.5 AU, would likely go undetected in the data. 
However, if Planet X were located further out in the solar system, beyond the orbit of Neptune, its mass could be constrained with greater accuracy. 
For instance, the mass of Planet X's orbit could be limited to the equivalent of 1.5 Neptune masses with a 90% confidence level. 
Given that the mass of a large Kuiper Belt Object is typically very small, our analysis suggests that most large Kuiper Belt Objects go undetected in the data, with only the most massive ones, with masses comparable to Neptune, having a chance of being identified.

Previous studies have demonstrated that Translation Memory (TM) can enhance Neural Machine Translation (NMT) performance. Unlike existing approaches which rely on bilingual corpora for TM, our work explores the use of monolingual data. We propose a simple yet effective technique to incorporate a monolingual corpus into the NMT model with minimal modifications. This proposed method significantly improves NMT performance with little need for hyperparameter tuning. Interestingly, even a relatively small monolingual dataset of 100 million bytes can yield substantial gains, achieving a 1.5 order-of-magnitude improvement over a strong baseline when translating low-resource pairs.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, namely low-variance circles and an unusual feature known as the "Carpenter Valley," could be remnants of the previous universe. These anomalies, when analyzed statistically, have a very low likelihood of occurring by chance, giving them a 1 in 10 million probability. Notably, these features align with predictions of the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology theory, which proposes the universe recycles itself in endless cycles, fundamentally differing from the standard Big Bang theory in how it interprets these observations.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing a Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands that study by establishing the convergence of the flow under certain data conditions within a broader category of data, identified through equivalence to conformal Riemann surfaces and showing the flexibility to handle more complex initial data than those previously examined.

To recognize new categories from minimal labeled data, few-shot learning has been rapidly evolving in recent years. However, traditional methods that rely on average operations for calculating prototypes often struggle due to the influence of outliers. This research proposes a new, effective framework that utilizes an episodic prototype generator module to create more representative prototypes from limited support data, reducing the impact of outliers and resulting in preferable models. The proposed framework is evaluated against various baselines on the widely used miniImageNet dataset, with the results showing significant improvements over existing methods that use average operations, particularly in the 5-way 5-shot and 10-shot scenarios.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the cold-start problem and improving single-domain recommendation performance. However, most existing research focuses on homogeneous single-source data, which cannot handle the challenges posed by sparse and disparate single-source and cross-domain data. In addition, implicit user feedback information, crucial for capturing preferences, is rarely considered. To address these issues, we introduce a novel, heterogeneous single-sparsed-domain recommendation framework called Enhanced Comprehensive Aspect Preference Learning (ECAPL). This framework is capable of leveraging implicit user feedback information to pre-process single-domain data and explicitly model user preferences across multiple domains to address the cold-start problem. Furthermore, we introduce a heterogeneous information propagation mechanism to transfer rich information across domains and enhance the precision of recommendations. Extensive experiments on real-world real-world datasets validate the superiority of our method over existing approaches, which not only resolve the cold-start problem but also achieve accurate recommendations for hot items.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools like barrier functions and active set methods. This paper introduces an algorithm designed to transform the solution process of a conic formulation into that of a related, more straightforward method by applying duality principles and a specific technique to a broader range of cones. We showcase the results of this method through the development of a custom software system and related advancements in the open-source Hamlr software library.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates the automation of quality control to efficiently manage triage and flag substandard scans for manual review. This study introduces a pioneering framework for evaluating the capacity of learning methods to generalize from a limited set of quality control labels to a vast set of unlabelled scans. Utilizing both conventional and cutting-edge, self-supervised, self-trained, and unsupervised approaches for classification, this research assesses their efficacy in effectively managing unlabelled scans. Furthermore, it identifies optimal techniques to combine these methods to improve performance on scans without existing quality control labels. With a limited set of training data, this quality control problem presents significant challenges in terms of diversity and consistency. Consequently, several methods fail to display reliable generalization abilities. However, combining a trusted classifier with an ensemble of high-dimensional cluster centers proves successful in accurately estimating scan quality.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation and energy networks.

Intel Optane DC Persistent Memory modules, supported by the user-space file system IPMI, have been extensively examined to understand their capabilities and limitations, ultimately revealing the most suitable scenarios for adopting this type of memory. Our findings show that Optane DC's throughput significantly surpasses that of SATA SSDs in both read and write operations in unstructured tests, with a notable 10x advantage in read operations. In contrast, NVMe SSDs demonstrate superior performance in all areas. Notable results also include the Optane DC's ability to match the latency of RAM in 4KB sequential read operations, surpassing the same in 64KB. Furthermore, our tests highlight the most efficient ways to utilize Optane DC, such as performing frequent small-scale read operations or occasional large-scale 1MB+ write operations.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal that this extension exhibits a complex pattern indicative of a strange attractor.

This research examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 (x = 1, 0, 0.5) using first-principles methods within the DFT framework, employing the Full-Potential Linearized Augmented Plane Wave method. We investigated the Full-Potential Linearized Augmented Plane Wave method using the Full-Potential Linearized Augmented Plane Wave method. Initially, our study of GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 (x = 1, 0, 0.5) was conducted using the Full-Potential Linearized Augmented Plane Wave method. GdSn3 and GdxCm1-xSn3 (x = 1, 0.5) showed good agreement with experimental lattice constants, while CmSn3 required adjustment of the Raman potential to match experimental data. Our analysis of the GdSn3 and GdxCm1-xSn3 (x = 1, 0.5) phases indicated a coexistence of localized 4f and delocalized sp-band electrons. In contrast, CmSn3 displayed overlap between inner 5f and outer s-p-bands. Our research further revealed that both GdSn3 and GdxCm1-xSn3 (x = 1, 0.5) maintained their

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental symmetry group from $SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ to $SU(4)_L \times U(1)_Y \times E_8$, a more comprehensive symmetry group that was once considered in the early developments of the unified theory. This theory, known as the unified linearly extended standard model (ULESM), suggests the existence of heavy bileptons with a mass of approximately $10^{16}$ GeV, along with a range of other particles that include heavy photons, gluons, and various types of quarks, leptons, and their respective antiparticles and partners with a mass spanning from a few TeV to $10^{16}$ GeV. The bilepton model and its associated unified theory are also examined in the context of their initial and laboratory-based production and detection methods, with the latter being most feasible through specific bilepton decay processes during the stages of the high-energy collisions expected in the high-luminosity LHC era and the future circular colliders like the high-energy LHC and circular collider. The paper additionally discusses the potential production and detection methods of the heavy photons predicted by the bilepton model and explores the conditions under which they could be created during the stages of the high-energy LHC and future circular colliders, and also discusses the potential for laboratory-based production of the heavy bile

The concept of ordered generating sequences for finite abelian groups is well-established, but this study extends that concept to finite Coxeter groups. A new definition of ordered generating sequences for the B-type Coxeter groups is provided, along with a corresponding basic theorem. The definition incorporates the partial order on the finite set of group reflections, and a fundamental result on the ordered generating sequences of the B-type Coxeter groups is proven. Additionally, explicit examples are given to illustrate the basic theorem.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset, we've discovered evidence that the galaxy cluster foreground influences a subset of the data. We've identified two key findings: firstly, SNIa behind galaxy clusters exhibit a 0.025 magnitude dimming on average, exceeding the expected 0.002 magnitude dimming from the lensing effect by typical galactic lensing. Secondly, we've observed a 0.04 magnitude discrepancy between the predicted and actual 1/Gyrs^-1 super-Novia effect, which could be attributed to the unanticipated 1/Gyrs^-1 effect of galaxy cluster lensing. By leveraging the extensive Pantheon data, we've produced a set of lookup tables that allow researchers to incorporate the 2Gyrs^-1 super lensing effect into their analyses of SNIa data.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations presented at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021. 

The main objective of these lecture notes is to provide an in-depth explanation of the variational method for monotone and coercive stochastic partial differential equations. 

The necessary background on Hilbert space-based functional analysis, operator theory, and stochastic analysis has been recapitulated within the lecture notes and further relevant references are included. 

The concluding chapter covers the pathwise approach to 2d Navier-Stokes equations.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks relies heavily on high-quality on-chip single-photon sources. Despite initial success in creating T defect sources in silicon, existing T sources fall short in both brightness and stability. A new method has been identified that involves creating T defects in photonic material by first etching a trench in the silicon layer and filling it with amorphous silicon. This method results in significantly enhanced extraction efficiency and more consistent performance compared to traditional implantation methods, as demonstrated by a 10-fold increase in brightness at a telecommunication wavelength.

MRI technology utilizes radio waves to scan the human body and obtain precise, pain-free diagnostic images. These images enable radiologists to visually assess anatomy and physiological processes within the body, ultimately facilitating early disease diagnosis and treatment. Advanced imaging capabilities, combined with sophisticated processing techniques, enable detection of hard-to-spot tumors. This assignment delves into Automated Tumor Detection by comparing conventional image processing methods, such as morphological analysis and regional growth algorithms, in order to explore their application and effectiveness.

In this research, we explore the properties of a novel algebraic variant of the degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$, as well as its corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number. This investigation is grounded in an innovative algebraic framework for generating functions and symbolic evaluation functions, allowing us to derive $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$. Our findings demonstrate intriguing connections with circulant matrices and Galois fields, while showcasing the potential for $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ to be applied in computationally efficient contexts.

The high accuracy goals of modern stellar spectroscopy are hindered by the presence of intrinsic noise from stellar activity, affecting the measurement of radial velocities. This study explores the impact of selecting different line sets on the residual stellar activity after applying least-squares deconvolution. It aims to mitigate the influence of activity on line profiles and understand the effects of increasing signal-to-noise ratios. A new set of algorithms was created to randomly choose line sets within specific velocity ranges, and the results show that more significant reductions in the width of residual features are achieved at higher signal-to-noise ratios with line sets from regions of large stellar activity variations. The findings also indicate that adopting a parametric line selection method yields better results than its unstructured randomised counterpart, and increasing the number of lines chosen leads to more substantial reductions in the residual features' width, as demonstrated with the Sun and an F-type star.

This research paper proposes a pair of methods for designing a flexible and efficient data collection process in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). The primary challenge addressed here is the overhead caused by sending individual confirmation messages from each node to a central node, known as a sink, during data gathering. To mitigate this issue, the first method divides the network's coverage into a hierarchical sector structure, allowing the sink to send a single command that covers multiple nodes within the same cluster. The first method is suitable for organized deployments where nodes know each other's positions. For unstructured deployments, the second method is used. It estimates the communication quality between nodes and the sink, and creates a linear order that maximizes the overall communication quality. Both methods are proven to be optimal or near-optimal through mathematical analysis and numerical simulations demonstrate their low cost efficiency.

For our task that depends on objects, it is crucial to identify and find the intended objects in a given scene, taking into account relationships between objects and their environment. Advanced neural networks like FANET and HRNet now have the ability to process context within images and are currently leading in objects that detect everything. In our study, the primary focus is on evaluating how these networks perform in describing context when used for deep objects detection. Using HRNet and FANET as our models, our work involves developing a context-aware system by incorporating object-oriented segmentation data into HRNet's architecture, as well as comparing it to FANet's context-aware mechanism. Our results show that modifying HRNet to include this kind of context knowledge led to improved HRNet-D context detector on the COCO dataset when evaluated using standard object detection metrics. However, in the more challenging COCO-FANet context detection evaluation, HRNet-D fell behind FANet in terms of performance.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations, which involves a given, non-positive function and a unique, bounded Bessel potential with an indeterminate upper limit. The system under consideration can be rephered to a Kirchhoff type elliptic system with a positively defined, non-singular potential exhibiting trivial upper limits in a particular Sobolev space. By applying a topological linking method and a critical perturbation technique, we establish the existence of at least one trivial solution and a corresponding non-trivial solution for the system in question.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube, subject to various forms of negative dependence, including independence and partial dependence. Our analysis yields new bounds for convex functions under such dependence structures, and provides comparisons with well-known bounds for independent and monotone functions. These new inequalities have beneficial applications in estimating the sizes of large deviations within the discrete cube.

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic greater than two, and consider the ring of power series $R$ over the Witt vectors of $k$, expanded in variables $t_1, \dots, t_d$. The main aim of this study is to generalize classical Fontaine-Messing theory to a base ring of the form $R$. Notably, we establish theorems enabling the comparison of crystalline and \'etale cohomologies with torsion coefficients for smooth schemes $X$ over $R$.

This study explores the transverse asymmetry in the azimuthal angle of hadronic pairs, arising from the interaction of transversely polarized targets with longitudinally polarized beams in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering. Our calculations incorporate various interaction mechanisms and reveal the sensitivity of this asymmetry to the target's transverse polarization and the intrinsic twist-3 distribution amplitudes of hadrons. As such, our findings suggest that measuring this asymmetry can contribute to testing the color antinterference hypothesis and provide insights into the spin structure of the target.

We've established recently that Fabre-Fock's coordinate system, a long-neglected component of General Relativity, offers an excellent framework for studying the geometry and physics of a de Sitter spacetime. Using a de Sitter hypersurface equation in Fock's coordinates, the intrinsic geometry of this space was found to align with previously published results, confirming the validity of this approach. Furthermore, the natural choice of global coordinates for describing a de Sitter hypersurface was demonstrated, with their metric providing strong evidence of the success of our method. Notably, the absence of singularities in Fock's coordinate system makes it an ideal system for representing the geometry and physics of a de Sitter spacetime.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes hyperlinks to rank and predict additional an entity's entities within the Yahoo! Knowledge Graph. We develop a node embedding approach, incorporating Wikipedia's layered structure and various edge types, to convert entities into low-dimensional vectors. Our method, COWIRE, considers different layers of Wikipedia, including redirect and type edges, to enhance entity representations. In evaluations, COWIRE consistently outperforms previous methods across different languages and datasets.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants arises from the incompatibility between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing number of list wait times. As a solution, cross-transplanting kidneys from donors whose kidneys have failed from patients whose blood can incompatibly match the waiting list patients can significantly reduce wait times. However, with the increase in complexity due to additional data such as urgency levels, organ functionality, and surgical risks, the decision on which kidneys to accept becomes crucial. This research aims to determine the most beneficial kidneys to accept to minimize the time spent on the waiting list by all involved parties.

Implicit copulas are the primary choice for analyzing dependencies in complex scenarios due to their ability to effectively model dependence in high-dimensional spaces. The most frequently used models include those based on quantile functions, like the Archimedean copula, as well as those based on distribution functions, such as the Gaussian and Student's $t$ copula. The parameterization of these models through a single parameter makes the estimation process more straightforward. The paper provides a comprehensive overview of the most widely used models, while discussing their applications and limitations, and discusses estimation methods, including maximum likelihood, Cramer-von Mises, and AIC, along with their performance in simulation studies. The article also explores the advantages and disadvantages of selecting implicit copulas in real-world data sets.

NLP techniques depend on representing words numerously, with success measured by task performance using datasets from sources like Loughran-McDonald. However, a deeper question arises: do these numerical representations accurately reflect the inherent meanings of words? To answer this, we used a dictionary-based sentiment analysis dataset and conducted a comprehensive examination of word definitions, semantics, and contextual usage. Our analysis of 1000 sample words with varying sentiment polarities was undertaken using human human evaluation methods, resulting in significant discrepancies between Loughran-McDonald's assigned polarities and the actual semantic understanding of these words. These findings were corroborated by machine learning evaluations. Our study's outcome is the first to provide empirical evidence of the native semantic structures of words from the English language's financial domain, with notable implications for developing more effective sentiment analysis models.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDET systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming strategy in [1].
Fair-throughput and sum-throughput optimisation problems are defined and formulated.
By leveraging an algorithm that utilizes fixed points, we derive the optimal SISO-OFDM system configuration.
Furthermore, with the assistance of global solutions from [1], we develop an efficient algorithm that yields the optimal MISO-OFDM system configuration.
Comparative analyses include simulations demonstrating the throughputs of SISO-OFDM, MISO-OFDM, and SISO-SLAM systems with various numbers of transmitters, specifically 1 and multiple, and several examples illustrating the equivalence of wideband and narrowband systems.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and high-resolution interface representation. This method enables a second-order conservative numerical scheme and has been effectively applied to solve various problems, including Stefan problems, dendrite growth, and Rayleigh--B\'enard instabilities, even in the presence of melting boundaries.

Current versions of the Lambek Calculus, used to model grammatical parsing, cannot effectively handle quantum-like phenomena present in language, specifically unary connectives. These phenomena occur when language cannot be interpreted linearly, such as the distributive phenomena resulting from interrogatives in the embedded context of statements. This study extends the classical Lambek Calculus by incorporating a minimal quantum fragment featuring interrogatives and statement embeddings, identified as QL-LC. This calculus facilitates the parsing of complex sentences with non-linear semantic structures through a combination of classical and quantum resources, demonstrated through analyses of sentence pairs involving interrogatives and sentences with modal operators.

In multiagent learning settings beyond finding equilibria, learning rationalizable actions is also essential. However, current algorithms in multiagent learning lack the ability to learn B-rationality in games with more than two players. This work presents an algorithm capable of learning $k$-B-rationality from independent data in games with more than two players when $k \geq 3$. The rationality level achieved by this algorithm is directly related to the sample size in the data.

An analysis of a stochastic Susceptible to Infective to Recovered model is conducted, where the model is based on an Erdős-Rényi random graph that changes dynamically as susceptible individuals connected to infected neighbours form new connections or sever existing ones. As the model is scaled to accommodate large populations, researchers found that the model's outcomes can be heavily influenced by a single parameter representing the ratio of new connections formed to the total number of connections in the network. When this parameter is less than a critical threshold, the epidemic may persist indefinitely, whereas above this threshold, the epidemic typically spreads rapidly and leaves most nodes isolated. This theoretical understanding is supported by numerical simulations.

In this study, we examine Cotton solitons within the context of almost Kenmotsu 3-$h$-manifolds. Initially, we establish the incompatibility of such solitons when the potential vector field is directly aligned with the Reeb vector field. Then, assuming the potential vector field is perpendicular to the Reeb vector field, we demonstrate the existence of Cotton solitons on almost Kenmotsu 3-$h$-manifolds, and derive a key characteristic equation for the potential vector field. Finally, we provide a specific example to illustrate our theoretical findings.

Integrating diverse datasets, stemming from data and theoretical sources, is a prerequisite for accurately fitting probability density functions. While aligning experimental data is straightforward, incorporating theoretical predictions poses a significant challenge. Discrepancies between the two datasets can be misinterpreted as either flaws in the theoretical predictions or as irregularities in the experimental data analysis. To circumvent this issue, an adaptation of the $\chi^2$ method is proposed, introducing an additional parameter to account for the disparity between the two datasets. Initially set to infinity, this parameter is gradually decreased, allowing for the fusion of the two datasets with increasing correlation. As such, a continuity scale is established, marking the point at which the two datasets are equal. From this point onwards, additional correlation may introduce noise into the data, rendering it unsuitable for PDF analysis. Thus, integrating the two datasets introduces a data quality metric, indicating how effectively the theoreical predictions can be integrated into the data analysis without introducing excessive noise.

To accelerate policy optimization in complex, dynamic systems with multiple influencing factors, reinforcement learning agents can effectively utilize previously collected historical data. Standard experience replay enables agents to retain information from prior iterations. However, the current approach equally values all collected observations, effectively mixing high and low quality information. In contrast, our proposed method, called Variance Reduction based Experience Replay (VFER), effectively reduces the overall impact of past information by giving less authority to the historical data. Building on the foundation of the standard experience replay, the VFER achieves the benefits of distillation while maintaining the ability to learn continuously. The proposed approach has shown substantial improvements, yielding a 15% enhancement in final performance and 30% reduction in optimization time in continuous control tasks. Furthermore, the VFER has been particularly beneficial when agents are trained on noisy data.

I'd like to introduce libcommute, a versatile C++11/14/17 template library that makes it easy to work with polynomial operators used in the quantum many-body theory by creating a specialized language for their manipulation. Additionally, it serves as a comprehensive toolkit for the development of exact diagonalization codes, carefully designed for high performance, ease of use, and code stability. libcommute boasts an intuitive syntax for commonly applied abstractions and can be customized with a Python interface, making it an ideal platform for developing and optimizing diagonalization codes. The library's efficiency and versatility has been showcased through the development of Speckie, a spin-chain solver, the code of which are publicly available at https://github.com/peh/ts/.

Establishing the electronic and superconducting gap structure of iron-based superconductors requires in-depth understanding of their complex multiband system. Resonant photoemission experiments have been employed to investigate these underlying structures in various samples of iron-based superconductors. Previously, researchers observed superconducting gaps in only the light hole bands in (Ba$_{0.6}$K$_{0.4}$)Fe$_{2}$As$_{2}$, whereas the electron bands displayed no evidence of superconducting gaps. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the electron and superconducting gap structures in (Ba$_{0.6}$K$_{0.4}$)Fe$_{2}$As$_{2}$ by measuring its photoemission spectra using photons of 47 eV and 66 eV. As a result, we discovered that superconducting gaps exist in all electron bands in (Ba$_{0.6}$K$_{0.4}$)Fe$_{2}$As$_{2}$, in contrast to the only superconducting gaps observed in the light hole bands.
