Recent research on block designs by Amarra, Devillers, and Praeger, involving specific quadratic polynomials, shows potential connections to two influential conjectures. The Bunyakovsky Conjecture would yield a crucial implication - infinitely many instances of the required designs. A vast number of prime values of the involved polynomials have been found and their quantities match closely the expectations based on a refined variant of the Bateman-Horn Conjecture. Although the infinite prime values of the polynomials have yet to be definitively confirmed, the results provide significant support for both the Bunyakovsky and Bateman-Horn Conjectures.

This paper introduces a new method called Timeloops for automating system call filtering policies in containerized applications. As containerization gains popularity in service-oriented systems, system call monitoring and system call filtering are crucial for the secure and efficient operation of these systems. However, manually creating system call filtering policies is a laborious and time-consuming process. To address this challenge, Timeloops uses a novel approach called system call policy learning, which automates the creation of filtering policies and ensures optimal performance and limited impact on system performance. Based on this approach, Timeloops is designed to containerize system call filters and use a customized containerization platform called Timely to concurrently train and evaluate multiple system call filter versions. Furthermore, Timeloops has been integrated with a popular containerization tool called Docker and is available for public use. Experimental results show that Timeloops can produce high-quality system call filters with superior performance to state-of-the-art methods and can significantly reduce the effort and time required to create system call filtering policies.

Investigating global $B-L$ symmetry within the Standard Model is necessary due to the anomaly cancellation requirements which necessitate three right-handed neutrinos that enable the natural generation of small Standard Model neutrino masses through the seesaw mechanism. Within an extension of the Standard Model featuring a $B-L$ symmetry, we introduce a pseudo-Goldstone boson dark matter framework where the scalar field responsible for pseudo-Nambu Goldstone boson dark matter acquires a vacuum expectation value at an energy scale of a few TeV. This model includes two distinct phases, the electroweak phase and the dark phase, with implications for the heat production and freeze-out processes of dark matter. By incorporating both direct detection scattering processes and indirect detection signals, we outline the characteristics of this model and provide constraints derived from existing experiments, including LUX-ZEPPININ, IceCube, and Fermi-LAT, as well as the Planck satellite's observations of cosmic microwave background radiation.

This study develops a Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM) filter where target appearance probabilities are organized on a grid. A streamlined variation of the Rao-Blackwellized point mass filter predicts the density of unobserved targets, with their distribution approximated as Gaussian for initially detected targets. Contrary to conventional implementations, the method presented here represents unobserved targets as a mixture of variation normals and Cauchy sources, achieved by integrating out measurement indicators within the exact prediction step using a novel integral solution. The approach is particularly beneficial in sensor management scenarios due to its ability to reduce the number of targets tracked individually, thereby decreasing computational expenses.

This study examines the null controllability of a population model that includes an interior degenerate diffusion component. By first establishing a new Carleman estimate for the adjoint system in its entirety, and subsequently deriving a relevant observability inequality, we aim to demonstrate the existence of a localized control action capable of driving the population towards extinction within a finite time frame.

The dynamics of soccer games mean even small moments can significantly impact the outcome, making players, coaches, and scouts intensely curious about how to act effectively in pivotal situations. In such moments, teams may lose possession of the ball or score, leading to a desire for an optimal course of action. To address this need, we propose a novel way to describe the game's state and a batch reinforcement learning approach to train a strategic policy network. By analyzing the contextual aspects of situations, the network can provide the best action to increase the team's chances of scoring, drawing on real-world soccer data from the 2013-2014 2017-2018 Bundesliga seasons for training. Experimental results show the proposed strategy outperforms the current approach in simulated scenarios, and we present two real-world examples of its superior performance.

High-resolution subsurface imaging is crucial in various applications, such as oil and gas exploration, and carbon dioxide storage monitoring. To achieve this, extended source (E-SWI) waveform inversion has emerged as a promising technique, effectively circumventing the computationally intensive cross-correlation step in traditional SWI methods. However, existing E-SWI methods are limited to small-scale problems due to the common approach of performing a zero-padding cross-correlation on the receiver data. In this study, an alternative strategy is proposed, where the source waveform is unrolled in the frequency domain rather than calculating the actual extended source data. This novel approach is shown to offer significant advantages, such as reduced memory requirements and enhanced computational efficiency, when combined with a source-internal parallel (SIP) parallelization approach. These improvements make the E-SWI method more practical and efficient, particularly in large-scale (3D) processing scenarios.

We've developed an all-optical technique for producing optical nonreciprocity on a microchip, achieved through the process of quantum squeezing a specific mode in coupled resonator systems. A key factor in this method involves applying classical coherent light in a one-way fashion to parametrically pump a nonlinear resonator. This selective pumping induces a chiral interaction between photons within the resonators, allowing us to build optical diodes and resonant nonmutual coupling systems. Notably, we've demonstrated the ability to produce ultra-high isolation ratios using resonant light and ultra-narrow linewidths, a critical feature for integrating photonic integrated circuits with dense connectivity.

We have presented the results from the AstroSat analysis of the high-mass X-ray binary X-ray pulsar IGR J19294+1816 during its Type-I outburst in October 2019. Timing and spectral data from the mission have been extensively studied. The spectral fitting revealed that the accretion disc is present, with inner edges located at 24-25 gravitational radii. The spin period of the neutron star remains unchanged at 10.5414(6) s. The light curve analysis detected a significant quasi-periodic oscillation at a frequency of 0.18 Hz, along with an equivalent width Hubble profile at 6.6 keV, which has been attributed to a cyclotron line. These findings have been compared to previous observations of this source, as well as other similar high-mass X-ray binary systems exhibiting similar characteristics.

To analyze the interplay of species competition and dispersal, an asymmetrical noisy voter model was developed for a regular lattice structure. The model allows one species to colonize nearest-neighbor sites, while another species can settle at any distance but is less successful in doing so. The model includes external noise, which can lead to random species swaps in the lattice. The combination of these dynamics results in various species competition outcomes, including the exclusion of one species, distinct population coexistence, or bistable coexistence dependent on the starting population ratio. The model shows that an abrupt transition occurs as immigration intensity surpasses a critical point, causing the abrupt transition is caused by an induced phase transition resulting from an abrupt change in the system's population due to an abrupt change in the system's population. Induced phase transitions, which are common in economic and ecological systems, are thus shown to be linked to abrupt species population shifts.

Ancient sundials served as primary timekeepers before the invention of mechanical clocks, with the classical Islamic civilization utilizing the Sun's daily movement to determine prayer times, often relying on local sundials for accurate timing. To address the lack of available research and available datasets on Indonesian sundials, this project aims to gather and analyze historical Sundial instruments, documenting their characteristics, origin, and functionality to utilize them as a reference for developing new, more precise timekeeping systems. The project involves a thorough examination of selected sundials, with detailed descriptions and graphical illustrations included to facilitate the development of more accurate time calculation algorithms, specifically for the region of Indonesia. This project is an initiative of the students from the University of Indonesia's Computer Science department, who are exploring the creation of a new Time Algorithm that could potentially be applied to Prayaa, a prayer time calculation system widely used in Indonesia.

This research focuses on an integrated data and energy transmission network, which incorporates D2D communication. In this hybrid network, a central hub utilizes a reflective surface to direct a data transmission in a specific direction, and captures energy from unused surface portions. We develop a surface configuration that maximizes the data transmission rate, and a power allocation strategy for prioritizing data transmission and charging, in a particular interval. This work formulates two optimization problems, which are resolved via a generalization of the Wolfenstein-Mie resonance behavior. Additionally, we integrate power and surface configuration to create a novel operation principle, which is verified via numerical simulations, and demonstrated to provide increased efficiency.

The surge in telework and distance learning has highlighted the benefits of telepresence systems that enable effective interaction with difficult-to-access areas. This is particularly relevant to Laser Doppler Velocimetry (LDV) systems, which are used for velocimetry studies. This paper presents the development of a telepresence system that enables an LDV system to acquire two-dimensional velocity measurements. The proposed system allows a user to control the LDV system from a remote location using a web interface, which has been implemented with the help of LabVIEW and an 8-channel LDV system. The system's functionality is demonstrated through its application in measuring the velocity field of a two-dimensional flow around a cylindrical object.

The effectiveness of programmable electrostatic phase plates in improving image
quality in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) has gained significant interest
over recent years. These phase plates, while promising, can introduce unwanted
aberrations that may hinder their overall performance. Through computer
modeling and experimental validation, we have developed a rigorous analytical
framework to evaluate the impact of two types of programmable phase plates on the
apochromatic TEM's point spread function (PSF). Our models indicate that one type
of programmable phase plate, referred to as Type A, can enhance the PSF's width
when the incident electrons have low energy or when used as an annular phase plate.
However, this plate may widen the PSF significantly when used as a circular phase
plate under these same conditions. In contrast, plates of Type B consistently
maintain their PSF width across all configurations, making them ideal as circular
phase plates for achieving high-resolution bright-field images. Notably, our findings
also suggest that a specific amount of astigmatism can further improve the PSF width
for electron energies between 0-10 keV when Type A phase plates are used in a
non-circular configuration. This opens up exciting possibilities for utilizing such
phase plates as programmable aberration correctors in TEM systems.

The success of data-driven dialogue models relies on their ability to accurately capture the nuances of human conversation. For an encoder to achieve this, it must effectively capture the essential elements of language that drive the task at hand, like holding the sender's identity in a multi-turn dialogue. We investigate whether this is possible for state-of-the-art encoders when evaluating their performance in multi-turn identification tasks, like in the DAMSL dataset. Our experiments, particularly those using controlled datasets with varying levels of complexity, show that current encoders struggle to encode everything needed for certain tasks, like distinguishing between different conversation participants, even with the help of attention mechanisms. Can simpler, more basic models surpass this limitation?

Deep learning methods for LiDAR data analysis have revolutionized 3D place recognition in autonomous vehicles and robotics by improving local re-localization and loop-closure detection rates in complex environments. However, extracting robust 3D features from LiDAR data remains a challenge due to variations in resolution and the difficulty of creating labeled datasets for evaluation. To address these issues, we present an innovative approach called AttDLNet, an attention-based single-shot LiDAR place recognition network. This approach utilizes a graph-based encoding strategy and an attention mechanism to automatically emphasize relevant 3D features, allowing for loop-closure detection in complex, real-world environments. We evaluate AttDLNet on the KITTI road scene dataset and demonstrate its superior performance, achieving a high loop-closure rate and low place error rate, even in cases of 90-degree LiDAR rotation. Additionally, we showcase the versatility of our approach by successfully applying it to real-world data collected from a real autonomous vehicle.

Streaming high-quality video, whether it's Video-On-Demand or live, demands transcoding to meet viewer demands and utilize limited broadcasting resources effectively. This study models video transcoding performance for both scenarios, considering the use of heterogeneous cloud services. The research develops a transcoding service model that accounts for multiple transcoding quality levels, each with its own resource and demand characteristics. By integrating this model with cloud transaction protocols, the research provides a transcoding system's average response time formula. The system's and model's effectiveness are demonstrated through numerical examples and comparative analyses using real-world video data.

We have derived a semi-analytical formula for the dynamic density-density correlation of massless Dirac electrons in doped graphene, which is applicable at finite temperatures. This finding is key to understanding the thermal screening of interactions among Dirac electrons and we leverage it to calculate the thermal capacity and compressibility of doped graphene. Notably, at very low temperatures, the thermal capacity displays a linear temperature dependence characteristic of normal Fermi liquids, with the coefficient controlled by the velocity of charge carriers in the material.

Continuous speech leads to consistent prosody patterns, yet current speech synthesis models often neglect contextual elements, resulting in monotonous outputs. To address this gap, we propose MaskedSpeech, a context-aware synthesis model that utilizes masking strategies to incorporate non-verbal information. By applying strategic masking, MaskedSpeech can generate speech with varying speeds and intonations, allowing it to convey emotions and attitudes. Experimental evaluations demonstrate MaskedSpeech's effectiveness in emotion expression and naturalness, outperforming baseline models. Furthermore, MaskedSpeech's flexibility in handling different masking strategies makes it adaptable to a wide range of applications.

We provide explicit definitions for the spectral and orbital stability of solitary waves in a model that includes a Klein-Gordon equation and an anharmonic oscillator. We also conduct a comprehensive analysis of the linearized equation's spectrum at the solitary wave state.

Q-ball studies in a single symmetry theory are common, yet the field can be more expansive, allowing for the examination of theories featuring multiple symmetries in a more general context. In this paper, we explore this broader scenario, analyzing both the standard and advanced limits within this theoretical framework and identifying essential conditions for existence in the more complex scenarios. Additionally, we identify a previously unexamined Q-ball state, which we term 'cored', and demonstrate that it could possess stability under specific conditions; a more detailed investigation into its implications will be addressed in a subsequent study.

We investigated a cyclic universe containing holographic dark energy with different infrared cutoffs, excluding the Big Rip singularity. The study reveals that, in the absence of interaction between the cosmos sectors, the HDE model using the Hubble radius cutoff behaves like a cosmological constant within cyclic cosmology. Furthermore, we discovered that cyclic patterns of contraction and expansion may be triggered by the energy density fluctuations of the HDE with the Hubble radius cutoff. We also examined the impact of inter-cosmic singularity energy transfer on the HDE's critical exponents in cyclic cosmology.

Gnutzmann and Smilansky previously developed a formula for the bond scattering matrix of a graph using a Hermitian matrix, for which an alternative proof has been devised, employing a method related to the zeta function of a graph. Furthermore, the formula has been broadened to cover regular coverings of graphs, and a novel 'L-function' concept for graphs has been defined, yielding a determinant expression. This has a corresponding outcome where the extended Gnutzmann and Smilansky formula can be represented by the graph's 'L-functions'.

We derive new conclusions regarding the additive Galois module properties of specific wildly ramified finite non-abelian extensions of Q. Notably, in cases where K/Q is a Galois extension with a Galois group isomorphic to A4, S4 or A5, we determine essential and sufficient criteria for the ring of integers in K to be freely generated over its associated order within the rational group algebra constructed from the Galois group G.

In experiments at Belle and Belle II, algorithms used to identify particles can miss the rare occurrence where an almond-like particle, produced in one part of a meson decay, remains undetected while its partner is found elsewhere. This phenomenon, where an ALP is produced invisibly, can be constrained by comparing experimental data with theoretical predictions for specific decay processes, such as when a beauty meson decays into an almond-like particle and other detectable particles. At Belle II, the expected sensitivity to detect these invisible ALPs is significantly improved, with some processes potentially observable at a level of one part in a billion over the course of five years of data collection.

This study provides a detailed examination of the potential inaccuracies in
the output of contextualized language models when analyzing diachronic word
representations. Our findings suggest that familiarization-based embeddings
may actually be more dependable for this type of analysis than anticipated.
We suggest revising the contextualized representations through a simple
normalization process to better align them with a consistent geometric
structure, thereby significantly boosting their performance in capturing
semantic shifts -- an average of 18% improvement over the previous
contextualized methods. Furthermore, our enhanced contextualized
representations achieve an average F1 score of 84.5%, exceeding even the
best-static baseline's 78% average F1 score in detecting semantic changes.
Our code is freely accessible on GitHub: https://github.com/fguadarrama/csc-
benchmarks

Active galactic nuclei (AGN) can be categorized into two types based on the spin of their central black holes: type-A with high-spin black holes and type-B with low-spin black holes. Recent research has established a correlation between ULTRA-luminous X-ray sources and AGN, revealing that most ULTRA sources are associated with high-spin black holes. This observation implies thatULTRA can serve as an indicator for the detection of certain ULTRA-luminous radio galaxies, which are expected to emit a distinct spectral feature caused by the interaction between a high-spin black hole and its surrounding plasma. The spectral line can be extremely narrow and may escape detection with conventional radio telescopes. However, it is projected that next-generation instruments such as the next-generation Very Large Array and the Korean Very Large Array will be capable of identifying this feature and could potentially identify numerous high-spin heavy radio quasars in the early universe. The detection of these high-spin heavy radio quasars would in turn provide evidence for the existence of certain ultra-light bosons, which are inconsistent with the mass range of certain ultra-light particles.

A distinctive feature of neural development is the rhythmic shifting of cell nuclei
between the upper and lower layers of the neuroepithelial tissue as interkinetic nuclear
migration proceeds, ultimately bringing the nuclei to the surface where gene transcription
occurs. The zebrafish retina offers an excellent opportunity to study the complex process of
interkinetic nuclear migration (INM) thanks to the availability of high-resolution live imaging
techniques. By using high-speed light microscopy, we recorded the vertical movement of nuclei
during INM in a zebrafish retina and found that the distance traveled by each nucleus varies
based on its position within the developing tissue. Notably, we found that nuclei in the upper
layer tend to move to the middle layer, while those in the lower layer move to the upper layer.
To gain insight into the underlying mechanisms of INM, we developed a new statistical model
that accounts for the directional bias present in the process. Through this model, we were
able to derive precise estimates of switching probabilities in the model, as well as the average
distance traveled by each nucleus during its cycles. Our results suggest that INM follows a
specific pattern that is best explained by a stochastic process with varying parameters, and
that this process is closely related to the overall development of the zebrafish retina.

In various image processing tasks, including video compression, demosaicing, and Compressed Sensing, the initial step involves compressing or removing data from images, with subsequent algorithms like Compressed Sensing and MoSAIC relying on test-time optimization to sort out source separation. However, these approaches necessitate Compressed Sensing's time-consuming phase-by-phase reconstruction and require a high compression ratio to produce satisfactory results. In this paper, we propose an alternative approach by optimizing an image model with a compressed linear transform to achieve optimal testing outcomes. Specifically, we introduce two optimized transforms called DEMOSA and COMPRE, which respectively cater to demosaicing and compressible video reconstruction. These methods achieve a high level of compression without compromising the need for a highly complex image model. DEMOSA and COMPRE demonstrate superior demosaicing and video reconstruction performance, yielding PSNR scores of 34.4/34.3 for demosaicing and 30.8/30.6 for compressible video reconstruction, at compression ratios of 4/4, surpassing the equivalent testing-level optimized counterparts.

We've developed a comprehensive hydrodynamic theory that applies to polar active fluids in the presence of randomly distributed inclusions, and our model demonstrates the possibility of overcoming these obstructions to maintain a non-zero overall speed. Contrary to previous assumptions, the dynamics of this specific class of active matter cannot be accurately captured using simplified hydrodynamic models when the spatial environment is two-dimensional up to five-dimensional space; however, we were able to derive precise, dimension-dependent scaling parameters for these dimensions.

Researchers within the same institution often rely on their institutional email as their primary means of communication, which can pose a security risk if compromised. As part of an in-depth analysis, we created and examined several institutional email communication networks, focusing on a specific case study at Jilin University. Our research identified critical vulnerabilities in research and development teams by exploring the structural weaknesses in these teams. We also investigated how network shifts impact these vulnerabilities, developed an efficient algorithm to find this structural information, and developed a effective method for pinpointing emails with high vulnerability. Our algorithm was able to identify this information accurately with high precision. Ultimately, our work provides a crucial foundation for enhancing team security and managing risks associated with institutional email communication.

Inspired by the pseudogap phenomenon in cuprates, a new class of electronic structures called exceptional van Hove singularities is identified within the framework of many-body theory.  The traditional classification of Hamiltonian eigenvalue coalescences is expanded to include this new category, and the pseudogap phase of certain high-$T_c$ superconductors is suggested as a potential manifestation of exceptional van Hove singularities.  Theoretical models based on Gutzwiller projection and atomic limit theories are utilized to analyze a specific $t$-$p/d$-$U$ Hubbard model, and demonstrate how exceptional points can arise due to interaction-induced symmetry breaking, and self-energy effects, and create a separation in spectral weight, and an anomalous charge carrier distribution that mimics the pseudogap, and nested-Fermi surfaces observed in experiments.  Moreover, a first-principles analysis of the copper-oxide plane in cuprates and a $p/d$-wave self-consistent analysis of the Hubbard model indicate that exceptional singularities can be attributed to electron-electron interactions overcoming crystal field splitting and bandwidth, and result in a distinct spectral weight separation, and nested-Fermi surface morphology. This paper details a specialized apparatus built for use in Aberdeen Tunnel's laboratory in Hong Kong. The laboratory is uniquely situated to study spallation neutrons produced by cosmic-ray muons with 611 meters of water equivalent in depth. The apparatus consists of six layers of horizontal plastic-scintillator detectors that pinpoint the direction and location of incoming muons. Between these layers, a neutron sensor filled with 650 kilograms of liquid scintillator containing a gadolinium dopant significantly enhances detection efficiency of the produced spallation neutrons. Additionally, we describe the apparatus's performance after upgrading it to a six-layer configuration and present initial data on muon flux, spallation-neutron production rates, and secondary neutron spectra.

This paper investigates the normalized ground state solution for the following biharmonic Choquard type equation: $\epsilon^4\Delta^2u+\beta(x)u=|\{u\cdot\tau_{f(\cdot)}\}|^{q-2}\tau_{f(\cdot)}$ where $|\{u\cdot\tau_{f(\cdot)}\}|$ is defined by the integral $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}\tau_{f(x)}|u(y)|^q\tau_{f(y)}dydx$ with $q$ taking the value $2(N-4)/(N-2\alpha)$, $\beta(x)$ being a potential function that may lose its uniform positivity, and $f(x)$ being either an exponential critical nonlinearity or an inverse square vanishing at the origin kernel, and $\tau_{f(\cdot)}\in H^2(\mathbb{R}^N)$, and $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u|^2dx=1$. By employing the truncation technique, concentration function method, and fractional chain rule, we establish the existence of a normalized ground state solution for the given equation.

Ground-based observations of planetary transits and radial velocities significantly improve the data from space missions like Kepler and TESS, enabling the detection of smaller planets that were previously undetectable. The TESS spacecraft has identified over 60,000 candidate exoplanets, making the selection of prime targets for follow-up studies a complex task. The TESS Force, a volunteer team of astronomers, aims to establish a robust and diverse program using the Keck/IKE telescope to gather data on the selected targets. The team is defining the scientific goals of this program and developing a reliable method to score and select prime targets for observations.

The growth of information technology has necessitated the streamlining of data collection and processing, with a suggestion to adopt an electronic approach. To this end, the implementation of ID card extraction through the use of optical character recognition (OCR) was studied. Building upon this, a two-step process combining NLP for correcting OCR errors was proposed. Test cases were conducted on 20 randomly selected Indonesian citizen ID cards to assess the system's NLP-based idiolect approach. As a result, the proposed idiolect approach achieved 95% accuracy in identifying 18 out of 19 key elements of an ID card, surpassing the raw OCR output's 63% accuracy.

Quantum harmonic oscillators were computationally analyzed in their ground state with either steady-state driving forces varying in intensity or driving forces that changed over time. Calculations of position expectations were carried out for multiple scenarios of mass, angular frequency, and the lambda parameter in both cases. Constant driving led to coherent states, with theoretical predictions closely matched by both simulation approaches. A discrete-time lattice Metropolis algorithm was used to evaluate the imaginary time path integral for these simulations.

The Yarkovsky-O'Keefe-Radzievskii-Paddack effect significantly impacts the rotational states of small asteroids by exerting a net torque resulting from solar radiation reflected and re-emitted by the surface. As a consequence of this phenomenon, the rotation period of these asteroids gradually changes, which can be best studied through light curve analysis. This study aims to estimate the YORP acceleration experienced by three asteroids - 1992 SK, Geographos, and Toro - whose rotation rates have been well-documented. Using available data from the Minor Planet Center and astrophysical parameters from recent studies, we found the YORP accelerations to be $4.4^{+2.4}_{-2.1} \times 10^{-8}$ m/s$^2$, $1.4^{+1.4}_{-1.3} \times 10^{-7}$ m/s$^2$, and $2.1^{+2.0}_{-1.8} \times 10^{-8}$ m/s$^2$ for 19155 1992 SK, Toro, and Geographos respectively. We also explored how future missions, such as the proposed Hera mission to the Didymos-Dactyl system, could measure YORP accelerations with greater accuracy.

The youth are increasingly relying on Instagram to express themselves and engage in political discussions with peers, utilizing the platform's features such as stories to initiate conversations. Through analyzing the daily interactions between users on Instagram, we can create a dynamic social network that reflects both users' connections and their conversations. By examining this network, a small world structure emerges, with clusters forming that reflect users' close-knit relationships. Further research using story data shows these clusters align with shared interests, values, and backgrounds. Notably, users with more followers tend to have greater influence on the network's overall connectivity, while users with similar follower counts may have differing levels of influence due to the heterogeneity of their audiences.

We show that any subgroup of homeomorphisms of a compact surface that fix the boundary, whose action within the surface's interior is highly transitive, cannot be topologically compact when using the compact-open topology's inherited structure.

Precise stellar characteristics are vital for both astrophysical studies and understanding stellar systems. We analyzed the M-dwarf ultraviolet sample, a collection of 140 field stars with high-quality M-dwarf spectra from the NUV, obtaining effective temperatures, surface gravities, and metallicities. Our flux-calibrated spectra were used to derive these parameters, with a focus on iron absorption lines within 3600-3900 Å, which are unaffected by line-blending from sodium. Our derived temperature estimates were 200-300 Å higher than those from existing models due to the use of unblended iron lines. We derived surface gravities of log(g) = 3.8-4.5, with 60% of the sample having gravity estimates of log(g) < 4.25, a threshold for field M-dwarfs established by the Spitzer Infrared Transiting Survey. Our derived metallicities ranged from [Fe/H] = -1.0 to +0.5. We cross-referenced our derived parameters with existing literature and found our temperatures to be 50-100 Å higher than the 2MASS and 8MASS M-dwarf models. We verified our gravity estimates by comparing hydrogen line equivalent widths with existing literature and our temperature estimates by deriving a M-dwarf luminosity function with our data fitted to the 2MASS and 8MASS samples.

Confining modes to the edge of materials over a broad spectrum is an appealing property shared by photonics systems, particularly due to its long-standing presence in topological insulators and polaritons.  However, these phenomena generally permit unidirectional propagation, limiting their application in devices that require light to travel in both directions.  In this research, a novel concept is proposed where line waves, such as polaritons, can be confined to the boundary between two specially designed meta-surfaces, allowing for bidirectional propagation.  Through a design based on coupled mode theory, it is demonstrated that a symmetry in the coupling strengths between the two meta-surfaces leads to line-confinement of both types of line waves.  This concept is then applied to create a compact polaritonic wave splitter using aluminum plasmons, showcasing sub-diffraction length losses and robustness against perturbations.

Although a key function in database management, query evaluation classification is well-established for various types of queries, the complexity of evaluating self-joined queries in relation to non-self-joined queries remains unclear. We set out to address this gap by examining the complexity of evaluating boolean self-joinedacyclic queries in comparison to both boolean and unanswerable non-self-joinedacyclic queries. Our analysis reveals striking parallels and distinctions in the complexity classifications across these categories, with some being equivalent, others analogous, and remaining areas for exploration. Moreover, our results highlight the critical role of query structure in determining evaluation complexity, providing the first complexity bounds for self-joined queries that are not acyclic.

Multiple models have been developed for modeling timed words, which are categorized as regular when their subset of regular functions are recognized by finite automata. This work extends the class of regular functions to timed words and offers a method for characterizing those in the extension using a logical framework. The characterization is based on a succinct representation in PTL with unique error conditions, which allows for a derivation of a synthesizeable deterministic finite automaton.

Researchers have analyzed collision data with an integrated luminosity of 3 inverse femtobarns, collected by the Belle detector at the KEKB accelerator. By studying a specific set of events where the $B^0$ meson decays into a pair of $K^{*0}$ particles, they have calculated the branching fraction for this decay process. This calculated branch fraction was found to be $0.41$ femtobarns, which aligns with the predictions of theoretical models and previous studies conducted by other experiments.

A machine learning technique known as reservoir computing generates a model that mimics complex systems and can be trained on significantly smaller amounts of data compared to alternative methods. The latest version of this approach simplifies training by minimizing the need to adjust numerous parameters. In a recent experiment involving a highly complex system with distinct time scales and multiple coexisting patterns of behavior, a reservoir computer of the new design demonstrated several advantages over its traditional counterpart. Specifically, it used a much smaller amount of data for training, a much shorter time to adjust its performance, a smaller number of parameters to adjust, and a much higher level of accuracy in predicting patterns of behavior, even when those patterns change rapidly. In addition to this performance, it was able to predict areas of stability accurately, further confirming the benefits of this new algorithm.

A new bias-corrected estimator has been created for the mean absolute deviation of a median regression model, addressing the problem of irregularity that typically hinders conventional bias reduction.  To overcome this limitation, a specific alternative strategy was implemented.  Establishing the bias correction involves verifying the local asymptotic normality property and a specific Bahadur-Kiefer representation.  Developed within the context of a traditional asymptotic framework, this proposal appears to retain effectiveness in high-dimensional settings, as evidenced by simulation results.

To address scalability issues with Eulerian methods for finding optimal controllers under constraints and worst-case disturbances in variational Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs formulations, we've developed a second-order successive sweep algorithm for calculating the reachable state space. This approach, which assumes a continuous and smooth Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation, enables us to determine the states that can be reached within a given time frame under worst-case conditions and state feedback control.

Multilayer Perceptrons (MLPs) have long been utilized as a baseline for comparing more complex models, but their efficiency has often been disputed. In contrast, we demonstrate that an optimally configured MLP framework can effectively serve as a local functional representation, outperforming state-of-the-art models with similar architectural features on the BAbel benchmark. Our optimal configuration is referred to as a Periodic Activation Modulated Network (PAN). PAN builds upon a standard periodic weight configuration, known to be robust across various tasks and data types. Notably, our research reveals that minor enhancements to an already optimal system yield negligible performance gains. Furthermore, PAN surpasses alternative optimization methods when applied to fully dense networks. Notably, PAN achieves remarkable performance with minimal parameters - around 1.2M - on the BAbel benchmark, matching the accuracy of large-scale transformer models with significantly more parameters.

The underlying structure of the brain's animacy organization in the ventral temporal cortex (VTC) across a diverse group of 15 healthy young adults remains unclear. Using structural MRI, we conducted MRI-fMRI analyses to examine the resting-state functional connectivity (RSFC) patterns associated with an animacy network (AIN). Our findings reveal that the AIN is consistently located in VTC and exhibits RSFC relationships with regions in the medial temporal lobe and prefrontal cortex. Furthermore, our MRI-EGLS analysis shows that the strength of connections within the AIN correlates with animacy-related patterns activation in VTC. The study implies that the animacy organization in the VTC may be rooted in the resting-state functional architecture of the brain.

The study proves the nonexistence of Landau-Siegel zeros or confirms quantum unique ergodicity for GL_2 Hecke-Maass newforms at a calculable pace, supported by the broader conclusion that Dirichlet L-function zeros exert a force pushing zeros from all other automorphic L-functions off the s=1 axis.

We have adapted the quantum relational Hoare logic originally proposed in (Unruh, POPL 2019) to incorporate "expectations" into preconditions and postconditions, thereby enabling the quantification of partial functions and the analysis of programs that may yield multiple outcomes.

The rapid dissemination of contagious diseases is frequently accelerated by a single major outbreak, or super-spreader event, where a single individual engages a notably high number of other infected individuals. Through a modified SIR model that accounts for this phenomenon, we examine the effects of high-scale infections on the overall spread and structure of an epidemic at a particular moment. By analyzing results from the model in relation to real-world examples of COVID-19, we observe that taking into consideration the effect of high-scale infections can provide more realistic predictions.

Let's consider a complex topological vector space, denoted as X, along with the collection L(X) of continuous linear operators that act on X. This paper seeks to expand the concept of codiskcyclicity, initially developed for a solitary operator within L(X), to a broader context of operator sets defined as $\Gamma\subset L(X).$ Some key results regarding codiskcyclic collections of operators are proven, accompanied by a codiskcyclicity criterion. Furthermore, we demonstrate its practical utility by investigating the codiskcyclicity of C_0-semigroups comprised of operators.

The paper addresses the problem of bias in vector magnetic field measurements obtained from solar images, a significant issue that hampers data analysis and modeling. While researchers have made considerable efforts to mitigate this problem in various inversion methods, the complexity of the corona still poses a considerable challenge. To tackle this problem, the authors focus on a commonly used metric, BER, and examine its behavior in a specific region, the active region AR12673, using a series of synthetic tests. By analyzing the bias in both magnetic field and flux calculations as a function of a specific parameter, the authors use visualizations and statistical tools to identify patterns. The results indicate that a widely-used weighting scheme exacerbates the effect of bias on the commonly used performance metric, BER. As a consequence, the authors propose using an alternative scheme, which demonstrates improved robustness to model bias in the examined region.

We present a novel, direct method for calculating the decay width of hadrons
decaying to two photons, utilizing quasi $\eta_c$ as a case study. This novel
approach differs from traditional methods, which involve virtual VMD and three-point
correlators, in determining the electron coupling constant, $ee\pi\pi$. By applying
an equal-time condition to a two-point correlator, we can derive the electronic
coupling constant, thereby enabling the calculation of lattice QCD predictions for
hadronic decays to two photons. This method is aligned with the physical process
and satisfies unitarity through the application of the K\"all\'en-Lehmann
spectral representation. Using this strategy, we were able to derive a precise,
accurate estimate for the lattice QCD prediction for $\eta_c\rightarrow 2\gamma$,
specifically $\Gamma(\eta_c\rightarrow 2\gamma)$, with a value of $5.2(4)(3)$ keV,
which can be traced back to recent lattice QCD calculations for the $\eta_c$ mass
and the light meson decay constant, $f_\pi$. This study was conducted at a lattice

A sign problem encountered in Monte Carlo simulations beyond half-filling can be mitigated by transforming the integration path, but this transformation also affects the computational complexity of the terms involved. The proposed solution involves a neural network that learns an optimal path transformation specifically for the Hubbard model, allowing it to handle the sign problem more effectively than traditional methods. This results in a significant reduction in variance, particularly near the sign problem's critical point, while maintaining a balanced computational overhead. Notably, this approach only requires a substantial decrease in sample size to achieve a sample-size advantage over quantum Monte Carlo simulations.

This paper examines the relationship between integers that are y-friable (or y-smooth) and the Dickman function by initially focusing on the number of y-friable integers in specified intervals. A key result is obtained for intervals with a y-small endpoint, showing the number of y-friable integers to be approximately $\rho(-y\log(R/R'))$ times the interval's length, with the approximation holding when $R'/R$ is a constant and the result is new even for constant values of $R$ and $R'$. Moreover, the absolute difference between the estimated and actual y-friable integer counts is bounded by $O_y(R^{1- R'/R +\epsilon})$. However, the time complexity of proving this bound is $y^{O(\log(R)/\log\log(R))}$, which may be reducible to $y^{O(\log(R))}$ with further analysis. This finding implies a y-friable integer analogue to a previously established theorem. Alternatively, the y-friable integer counts can be estimated in $y^{O(\log^2(R))\log\log(y)}$ time. Finally, the paper also addresses y-friable integers with the restriction of being (ab)-perfection.

Given any non-erasing free monoid morphism σ and subshift X, its image subshift Y under σ and the associated complexity functions p_X and p_Y exhibit the following relationship: there exist constants c, d, and C, where p_X scales by a factor of at least c times d, while scaling by at most C, whereas topological entropy h_X satisfies a similar bounded ratio with h_Y, and this ratio is influenced by the logarithmic growth rates of the minimum and maximum lengths of words in Y representable with each length n. Additionally, for free groups, and subgroups u and v with finite index, the complexity functions p_{[u]} and p_{[v]} exhibit a similar bounded ratio, and this bound is further related to the maximum and minimum lengths of words in v expressible with each length n using the free basis of u, and this relationship yields a comparable one for topological entropy, and this and previous findings contribute to proving that topological entropy is invariant under pre- and post-composing with such morphisms or group basis changes.

By leveraging previously acquired skills and adapting them to unfamiliar tasks without explicit guidance, humans demonstrate impressive cross-task capabilities.
Similarly, our goal is to enable models to generalize beyond their trained scenarios and on continuous landscapes of related tasks.
In this objective, we focus on two key aspects: allowing the model to efficiently generalize to new, adjacent tasks and preventing it from achieving optimal performance on individual tasks by过分 specializing.
To this end, we develop a neural network system with cross-task generalization properties over a continuous range of tasks.

In addition, we employ a continuity regularization that ensures smooth transitions between tasks by adapting the model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model.
We experiment with multiple tasks, including syntax-dependent coreference resolution and natural language inference withcontradictory premises, and we show that our approach effectively adapts the model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model to a model

This research introduces M-arvedo-Kaczmarz, a novel variant of the ICA method for extracting non-gaussian independent components. The 'm' in M-arvedo-Kaczmarz is indicative of its suitability for low-precision arithmetic systems using 'm'-bit integers. The method builds upon the traditional ICA algorithm by integrating elements of the ICA and the reweighted Kaczmarz method for linear systems. The convergence properties of the algorithm are theoretically proven under specific conditions. The method's effectiveness and precision are validated through numerical experiments, particularly when 'm' is set to 8 bits. The implementation exhibits linear scalability and server-less operation when deployed with Apache Spark, the framework's capabilities are highlighted through a case study using data from the TIMIT corpus. The method's efficiency in handling a comprehensive dataset of 50,000 samples is demonstrated, resulting in superior performance compared to traditional centralized implementations of ICA and fPCA.

This work offers an overview of requirements engineering in the gaming sector.
Existing research studies on this topic have been comprehensively examined.
Key characteristics of the gaming industry were identified and their connections to broader market dynamics discussed.
In addition, several potential areas for further research within this field were briefly highlighted.

Optimizing hyperparameters in the private version of the stochastic gradient descent algorithm is a critical issue, as its performance is highly dependent on well-tuned hyperparameters. Given the vast number of hyperparameters to consider and the time-consuming nature of evaluating each one under privacy constraints, traditional methods fall short. To address this challenge, we present an optimized approach for finding the best hyperparameters for private deep learning models within a limited budget of evaluations. By focusing on two widely used models, we develop efficient search strategies that outperform standard hyperparameter optimization techniques. Our methods, which involve carefully selecting hyperparameters and using lower-dimensional parameters, lead to significant improvements in model accuracy, as demonstrated in our experiments.

For a Coxeter system denoted by (W,S), we develop the concept of a boolean complex consisting of involutions within W, mirroring Ragnarsson and Tenner's previous work. By applying discrete Morse theory, we identify the homotopy type of this boolean complex for a significant subset of Coxeter groups, including finite groups, revealing that its homotopy type is equivalent to that of a collection of spheres with dimension |S|-1. Moreover, we derive straightforward, recursive formulas to compute the number of spheres within this collection.

The Euclid satellite, set to launch in 2022, will significantly influence future cosmological research with its Visible and Near Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer instruments. The authors of this study analyzed how correlated readout noise affects in-flight measurements for the NISP detectors, characterized by their 15 micron pitch and H2RG readout noise properties. Experimental data indicates that for NISP, the impact of this noise on in-flight measurements will likely be minimal, with estimated values of -0.006 for the bias and 0.005 for the RMS on the signal-in-readout level. However, simulations suggest the impact may be slightly higher at -0.014 for the bias and 0.012 for the RMS. Euclid's advanced NISP sensors are expected to have a reduced impact of this noise compared to the Planck NIS instruments. Like NOLA, NOLB, and NOLC, the authors developed the SnRi method to estimate signal levels free of the readout noise's impact, with NOLA serving as the default and effectively limiting the additional correlated noise's effect to less than 10% of the shot noise.

We applied an advanced statistical approach using linear regression to analyze iron spectra from 8409 red giant stars in the Milky Way disk, drawn from the APOGEE-2 dataset. This allowed us to examine how elements such as alpha, iron-peak, and chondritic elements vary with metallicity. Our findings revealed three key relationships: the alpha/alpha correlation, the alpha/[Fe/H] correlation, and the [C/O] vs. [Fe/O] graph, all dependent on metallicity. These discoveries were validated by both observational and theoretical studies. We developed a statistical model to predict line intensities based on two chemical distribution factors and metallicity, which when compared to the data showed a very close match. Our model simplifies the complex chemical variations seen in the carbon monoxide graphs, the alpha elements beyond the [Fe/N] graph, and in general, the [El/[Fe/H]] graphs, where El denotes any given chemical element. Notably, our model can accurately predict line intensities, demonstrating that carbon abundance is influenced by both the [Fe/O] graph and the [Fe/N] graph, while other elements are primarily correlated with one of these graphs or metallicity alone. Leveraging our model's success, we created carbon, alpha, and iron-peak maps of the galaxy, and when we accounted for carbon abundance and the alpha enhancement graph, we found that iron alone accounts for less than a quarter of the chemical variation seen in the data

The COVID-19 pandemic in China sparked a variety of rumors, including those about government supply shortages, false claims of effective cures, and hoarded medical equipment. These unverified pieces of information led to widespread panic among the public. To better understand the spread of rumors, we analyzed search data from major Chinese search engines and identified four primary mechanisms of rumor propagation: cascading, coexisting, decoupling, and emerging types. Our findings indicated that different mechanisms of rumor spread had varying levels of influence, with a proposed model successfully capturing this pattern. Decision tree analysis revealed that the reach factor was the most critical in determining the spread mechanism of rumors, with implications for developing effective strategies to contain their dissemination.

A novel approach to measuring the distance to galaxies has been discovered by examining extragalactic planetary nebulae. Specifically, the method involves comparing the observed and theoretical brightness of planetary nebulae, which can provide a precise estimate of a galaxy's distance. To explore the distances to galaxies within the Fornax cluster, we have collected high-resolution images of 19 individual galaxies and identified 1024 planetary nebulae across them. By analyzing the data, we have obtained estimates of the distance to each galaxy and, in some cases, the error margins. Our findings indicate that our results are in line with previous measurements using different techniques and, in fact, offer a more precise assessment than the existing data in the Scylla2 catalogue. Additionally, a specific galaxy, NGC 1656, has been identified as potentially being two distances closer to the center of the cluster than earlier reported.

Every day, hospitals around the world gather vast amounts of physiological data from their patients, leading to an increasing demand for real-time processing and monitoring systems. To efficiently handle this data flow, a high-performance stream processing engine is essential for real-time analysis and reporting. However, existing high-performance stream processing engines are not optimized for the unique characteristics of medical data streams, which typically have low update frequencies, a high number of individual streams, well-known endpoints, and varying patterns. As a result, these engines experience significant overhead from stream management, performance modeling, and scheduling, ultimately leading to poor resource utilization and poor scalability. To address this challenge, we have developed LifeStream, a specialized stream processing engine tailored for medical data streams. LifeStream's key innovations, including stream multiplexing, lazy data processing, flexible scheduling, and adaptive scaling, allow it to effectively manage periodic streams, achieve linear performance scaling, and minimize latency, all while using significantly less computational resources.

This research paper confirms that certain types of curves, specifically those in higher dimensional space, do not fit the classification of Bertrand curves except in two-dimensional Euclidean space. A new category, called the timelike (1,3)-Bertrand curve, is defined to fill this gap and its characteristics are identified for curves in a four-dimensional Euclidean space.

The choice of loss function for a neural network is widely regarded as a key decision with far-reaching implications, given the numerous loss functions developed to date, making it crucial to carefully select one. Despite its significance, research on the topic often omits explicit justification for loss function selection. We contend that this lack of justification reflects an untested assumption prevalent within the deep learning community. In this research, we investigate how loss function impacts performance in a supervised classification context. Our findings reveal that the loss function's impact on model accuracy is closely linked to the nature of target class probabilities within the output space, allowing us to group loss functions based on their behavior.
A stabilizable boundary feedback controller is designed for the Navier-Stokes equations using a linear control scheme with an oblique boundary orientation.

This research aims to advance the understanding of thermomechanical behavior in polymer crystallization. Strain-induced crystallization plays a significant role in polymer mechanical and thermal properties and must be accounted for during production and final product applications. To effectively model this process, existing objectives have been identified as deficient due to their inability to reflect strain-induced crystallization's thermodynamics. To address this, the current study introduces a family of objective functions and conducts numerical simulations to evaluate the mechanical and thermal behavior of strain-induced crystallization in a 1D heat conduction scenario. The results indicate that the proposed objective functions can accurately capture the desired material properties when combined with suitable growth conditions, but the most suitable objective is still to be determined through further experimentation.

To understand the impact of spin interactions and single-particle excitations on the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a neutral quark plasma, we apply jitter theory to study the superconducting phase of the QPM. In this phase, jitter theory allows for the neglect of certain quasinormal modes, and we analyze the properties of a nematic superconductor, paying close attention to its gap structure. By examining the response of the superconductor to small perturbations, we discover that certain quasinormal modes correspond to specific collective modes, including the Higgs mode and a unique nematic mode. Furthermore, we investigate the spin properties of these modes and discover that the Higgs mode arises from interactions between quarks of the same charge, while the nematic mode results from the mixing of quarks of opposite charges.

One significant issue in Imitation Learning (IL) is that obtaining optimal feedback, such as demonstration data, can be quite costly and time-consuming in robotics applications. To address this challenge, semi-supervised IL has developed various feedback models that allow the learner to receive non-optimal feedback at a lower cost. Unfortunately, these models are difficult to calibrate in real-world robotics scenarios. In this paper, we introduce a novel setting where a learner can receive unlabelled data, along with the ability to receive corrective feedback, such as demonstration data, for selected selected data points. To make the most of this heterogeneous data, we developed a meta-algorithm that enables the learner to receive corrective feedback on a selected data points. The algorithm is computationally efficient, requiring only one learning step per data point and only providing optimal feedback for the selected points. The proposed method is straightforward to apply across different IL scenarios and currently, the algorithm's performance is demonstrated through several real-world grasping tasks.

Continuous phase modulation detection using conventional differential detection techniques is highly resistant to various channel disturbances, such as phase and Doppler shift. Its basic structure involves a memory of one symbol, which simplifies the decision-making process and reduces its computational cost. Nevertheless, enhancing the block length in optimized equalization can significantly improve the performance in channels with intersymbol interference. Our research indicates that introducing a block length greater than one symbol in a cost function, considering the direct current component and the block-length equalization technique, yields better performance for coherent detection methods. Interestingly, our results indicate that even a minimal increase in delay, such as 0.05 of a symbol, results in significant performance gains for modulation techniques like 4R-USDO and 8R-NRZ, bypassing the need for complex optimization schemes or advanced signal formats.

New findings from 1D core-collapse simulations have been found to align closely with their complex multi-dimensional counterparts within accepted stellar collapse models. This supports the notion of underlying universal principles governing the collapse of stars. Despite some discrepancies in the structure of ejected material due to differences in numerical methods and supernova mechanisms, this study reveals that fundamental properties such as total mass, average velocity, and energy loss timescale remain consistent across various models. These properties significantly impact the duration of chemical tails produced by the neutron-star explosion, which in turn affects the threshold for detecting black-hole neutron-star merger events. We utilize a simplified model to connect neutron-star deaths with these mergens, and based on a limited gravitational wave detector sensitivity, we determine that a specific detection protocol can be achieved if there is a certain energy loss range and velocity ratio. However, this range relies heavily on the actual sensitivity of the detectors, suggesting that with current limitations, it corresponds to an approximately 8 solar distance. We anticipate that improved sensitivity in the coming decade will be capable of distinguishing between different death models.

Current deep learning techniques for removing rain from images have achieved notable success, yet their assessment of performance remains limited due to the lack of real-world rainy data. To evaluate these algorithms on clear images, synthetic rainy data is usually created by visually adding computer-generated rain. This two-step process can introduce color and shape inconsistencies, along with misaligned rain elements. In contrast, our proposed approach learns to both generate and remove rain from images with actual rainy data, treating the process as reverse translation. By utilizing a disentangled translation framework, our model is capable of efficiently eliminating rain as well as controlling the elements of a artificially added rain in the output. Our method surpasses existing translation-based approaches using either a single generator or multiple generators in evaluating performance on standard datasets.

A prominent paradigm in reward learning utilizes human feedback via comparative evaluations, but their broader adoption is hindered by the expense and labor intensity of these comparisons. To overcome this limitation, we propose grouping multiple comparisons together and allowing human labelers to mark sub-regions of a condensed state space representation, thereby efficiently leveraging human time. Through data visualization techniques, we convert the encoded states from our comparator model into an image format that accurately reflects comparative relationships, facilitating rapid annotation through cluster ranking. Our experiments demonstrate that this innovative approach yields substantial improvements in sample efficiency while matching the performance of traditional comparative evaluation methods.

We discuss the impact of model theory on set theory, focusing on model companionship in the context of Tarski's higher-dimensional geometry axioms from 1915. This system, which initially had no provision for the unique continuation of geometric constructions, was later found equivalent to ZFC when applied to the complex plane. We re-examine Tarski's axioms through the lens of model theory to identify what can and cannot be derived, and explore the axioms' relationship to the continuum problem. Notably, we discuss how the model-theoretic property of eliminating quantifiers influences the size of the continuum. This connection has significant implications for set-theoretic methods, and we discuss a possible lower bound for the continuum based on the model-theoretic behavior of a specific formula. This line of reasoning suggests that the continuum cannot be smaller than $\aleph_1$ in certain models, and we discuss the underlying mathematical principles driving this conclusion.
This study establishes conditions and proof of existence for a modified Branson-Paneitz equation under Navier boundary conditions on a finite region of n-dimensional Euclidean space.

This study aims to assess the capability of the Five Factor Model (FFM) of personality to predict substance abuse risk. A comprehensive survey was administered to 511 participants in Italy, measuring their FFM personality traits on a dimensional scale from Neuroticism to Conscientiousness, along with their demographic information and scores from a drug consumption risk assessment tool based on the Five Factor Model of Personality (FFMCP). Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS 25, employing both descriptive statistics and linear regression. Results indicated that FFMCP scores could be successfully predicted by FFM personality traits, with the regression model showing statistical significance. Furthermore, FFMCP scores were found to be highly correlated with Big Five personality traits, with the strongest relationship observed with Openness to Experience.

Our proposed dataset, ATOMIC, is an exhaustive collection of everyday commonsense knowledge that encompasses over 100,000 pairs of conditions and consequences, along with more detailed information about 300,000 stories.  It includes various types of reasoning, including over 30,000 pieces of information that require a single step to deduce and over 100,000 pieces of information that require a chain of reasoning to deduce.  We have conducted experiments using several IF-THEN reasoning models, which demonstrated the necessity of taking into account both the conditions and the contextual background when trying to infer the underlying causal relationships, highlighting the power of machine learning combined with a rich, comprehensive dataset like ATOMIC.

Portfolio optimization is a complex task involving numerous interconnected decisions that are bound by specific constraints, making it particularly challenging to manage for financial institutions. Utilizing the QPE-based HHL algorithm for solving linear systems, we developed a novel approach to solve the expectation value problem in the HHL algorithm. By implementing our HISQL algorithm, we demonstrated the potential of listing and selecting items near term hardware, using a 20-qubit D-Wave system as our testing hardware. Our results show the capability of NISQ-HHL to handle portfolios comprising up to 15 assets, providing a robust and efficient solution to this critical financial problem.

To enhance data efficiency of state-of-the-art end-to-end ASR models and enable them to handle a large scale of data effectively, we introduce a multi-modal training approach that incorporates both unidirectional and bidirectional attention mechanisms. This approach leverages text data more effectively by utilizing pre-trained encoder models and adds a training stage that leverages high-quality text-data to refine the speech-data. We expand our proposal by introducing a bidirectional attention mechanism in our training framework. This framework is simple to integrate but yields a significant performance boost. Experiments on the Librispeech dataset demonstrate that this approach yields a 2nd rank improvement in Word Error Rate (WER) when compared to the current end-to-end ASR baseline.

This analysis addresses the challenge of optimizing cross-sectional area through a specific point within a geometric form. To generalize this concept, the approach is expanded across multiple dimensions. Nonetheless, the optimal average cross-sectional volume cannot be achieved unless cross-sections pass through the centroid of the shape. Therefore, the focus is on stationary shapes with optimal average cross-section properties. A new formula is introduced for average cross-section calculations in any dimension, and the associated equation of stationary shapes is derived. Characteristics of stationary shapes are discussed through mathematical derivation, numerical modeling, and graphical visualization. Additionally, the distinct properties of stationary shapes in 2D, 3D, and 5D are examined and analyzed.

This paper investigates the long-term behavior of a randomly generated uniform parking distribution of size $n$, specifically focusing on the asymptotic behavior of its first $k$ positions as $n$ approaches infinity. A uniform parking function of size $n$ is defined as an ordered sequence of non-negative integers that does not exceed $n-1$ and satisfies certain combinatorial criteria.

Measurements of superconducting nanowires, particularly NbN nanowires, indicate the presence of a critical voltage threshold for dc conduction below which coherent quantum phase slips dominate, a phenomenon that can be visually depicted in the data obtained from our three-parameter plot. The critical voltage threshold is distinct from the behavior observed in normal state resistance, and the conductance of the nanowires in this regime is influenced by the material properties and geometry of the device. The data also reveal the presence of a conductance maximum, which occurs at a specific voltage threshold and is higher than the conductance observed at lower voltages. The maximum conductance threshold is higher than what would be expected from a classical Coulomb blockade model, and the behavior of the nanowires in this regime is better explained by quantum phase slips, a phenomenon that arises from the disruption of the superconducting quantum phase due to external gating. The critical voltage threshold is lower in samples with thicker oxide layers, and the conductance of the nanowires in this regime is lower in samples with thinner oxide layers. The data also indicate the presence of a maximum conductance threshold, which occurs at a specific voltage threshold and is higher than the conductance observed at lower voltages. The maximum conductance threshold is higher in samples with thicker oxide layers, and the conductance of the nanowires in this regime is lower in samples with thinner oxide layers. The discovery of T-dwarf GJ 229B in 1995 offered initial insight into its composition, yet a detailed analysis with current spectroscopic methods has been lacking, especially concerning its atmospheric features which are complex. This study utilizes the APOLLO retrieval code to create the most precise model of GJ 229B's atmosphere to date, based on its observational data, with a focus on its spectral characteristics within the 0.8-5.1 $\mu$m range. By analyzing its distance, age, and luminosity, along with multiple possible scenarios, the study found that GJ 229B has a mass of 0.030 $\pm$ 0.005 $M_{\odot}$, an equilibrium temperature of 550 K, a semi-equilibrium temperature of 530 K, and that its spectrum is best explained by a mixture of silicate and FeH grains with a specific size distribution, along with a surface that is relatively uniform in color. Further analysis of its spectrum in the near-infrared range, however, points to a more varied surface color, indicating a possible discrepancy that could be explained by a more intricate atmospheric composition. This study also found that a detailed analysis of GJ 229B's spectrum, particularly its features in the 0.8-5.1 $\mu$m range, can be best explained by a specific temperature distribution of its

Our study investigates the properties of deep inelastic scattering when interacting with a quark-gluon plasma using color-dipole formalism, building on the Weizs\"acker-Williams approach.  By doing so, we can extract structure functions from the scattering cross-section and use color-dipole formalism to directly calculate these structure functions.  Our findings reveal discrepancies between theoretical predictions and data from the PHENIX experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider, particularly in regions of interest for nuclear physics research.  In contrast, our calculations more closely align with data from the HERA collider.  In addition, we explore the impact of including saturated quarks in our calculations and observe that it has a significant effect on the structure functions, with implications for the interpretation of experimental data.

Our proposed approach tackles the challenge of novel view video prediction, taking input from multiple viewpoints. Unlike existing research that relies on narrow angle variations, our network can generate videos from significantly wider angles, up to 45 degrees, without the need for prior knowledge. By processing only RGB frames, we've developed a two-component representation, combining local and global features that enables novel view prediction. Our model achieves remarkable results on real-world datasets NTU-RGB+D and CMU Panoptic, surpassing the state-of-the-art in novel view video prediction, demonstrating significant gains in SSIM, PSNR, and FVD scores of 26.1%, 13.6%, and 60% respectively, without the use of prior views.

In this research, inter-orbital coupling was demonstrated using femtosecond laser writing, which enables orthogonal modes in a photonic lattice to couple with each other at different spatial locations. We characterized an asymmetric double-well structure, mapped its propagation dynamics and successfully created a device that uses inter-orbital coupling for mode conversion. Furthermore, we showed that light with an linear polarization can be transformed into circular polarization. This transformation utilizes the S-to-P mode coupling in the photonic structure and has the potential to be used in future integrated photonic devices that require such mode and polarization conversions.

The Ω-baryon, which contains sss quarks and has only been marginally detected in past experiments, has primarily been studied using theoretical methods so far. A study aims to explore this particle's properties utilizing a quark model with linear confining forces. Calculated resonance masses are presented for the ground and excited states of S, P, D, and F quark systems. A linear nature of the Regge trajectory, supported by calculated data and magnetic moments, has also been examined. This study compares its results to other approaches and available experimental evidence.

Airborne transmission risk in confined environments like buses is intricately affected by the interplay between turbulent airflow, respiration processes, coughing, and sneezing, as well as various ventilation methods, temperature-driven natural convection, and surface exhalation. To better understand and quantify this complex dynamic, we used a computational, time-dependent airway transmission model to analyze the effects of sneeze droplets on a bus, assuming uniform droplet distribution as an initial condition. Our analysis revealed that while some smaller droplets may remain suspended in the air for an extended period, larger droplets tend to settle near the floor, forming distinct clusters. Notably, we found that simulated droplet patterns closely matched those obtained from a well-known simplified model, making the latter an effective tool for estimating transmission risks posed by aerosols in confined spaces like buses, trains, and other public transportation settings.

Building on cutting-edge experimental projects such as HIBEF at the XFEL, our calculations investigate the birefringent scattering of x-rays when interacting with two combined optical lasers, considering various possible outcomes. To aid in detecting quantum vacuum effects experimentally, our analysis focuses particularly on situations where x-ray photons show differences not just in polarization, but also in direction of propagation and potential energy changes.

This note outlines the algorithm devised by J. M. Eisenlohr and S. L. Farris to
systematically generate all fully transitive polyhedra in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Furthermore, this algorithm is employed to construct a novel polyhedron within three-dimensional Euclidean space.

Broadbent and Lord introduced the concept of unclonable encryption, a novel scheme that permits only novel copies of an encrypted message. This concept was subsequently explored by other researchers, who proposed various realizations of the scheme. However, these realizations fell short of being fully secure. In this research, we present a comprehensive and secure definition of unclonable encryption, a new construction achieving this definition in the random oracle model, and an alternative construction assuming macro-cloning.

This study confirms that physical layer-based authentication is achievable in
Gaussian noise environments, with the caveat that an all-knowing adversary cannot be
beated. We formulate an optimal classification model for the case in which the
adversary masquerades as either of two legitimate users. In this model, we
develop a method to identify the identity of the sender without having access to any
secret information. We prove that the optimal classifier used by the receiver is
the same as the one that minimizes the error rate. This means the receiver is
always able to correctly identify the sender, with the lowest possible error rate.
We also provide a method to simulate the behavior of the optimal classifier in
scenarios in which the channel conditions vary. This is done by showing that the
receiver's decision boundary can be simulated with a logistic regression model.
We also present several strategies to enhance the efficiency of these models.
We then simulate the performance of these models under different scenarios and
provide the results. Our findings indicate that the efficiency of the system
decreases linearly with the proportion of data that has been tampered with. This
means that the receiver's ability to correctly identify the sender drops
significantly when the sender masquerades as the other user. We also found that
the receiver's accuracy improves with the use of a more sophisticated algorithm.
